trip_context: {"Trip type": "Vacation", "Travel group": "Couple", "Hotel highlights": "Great view", "Bed comfort": "Neutral"}
text:
There are many accommodation options in Hoi An. After looking around, I decided to stay a bit further out, where there would be much less noise from people and vehicles. It's about a 15-minute walk from the hotel to the Old Town. If it's not raining, it's not far to walk along the riverbank or the road. However, September is the rainy season, so it becomes a bit inconvenient when it rains, as there will be standing water along the way, and the sidewalks are not in good condition, full of potholes and often blocked by cars and motorcycles.

Welcome snacks were provided upon check-in. The hotel's floors 2-7 are the accommodation area, the first floor houses the lobby, swimming pool, bar, and dining area, and the basement contains a gym and spa. I chose a river-view room, specifically requesting a high floor, and the hotel provided a second-to-top floor. The view at night was truly beautiful; the lights of the riverside houses and the moonlight reflected on the riverbank, with occasional small boats carrying lanterns passing by. Although there were occasional horn sounds, the soundproofing was decent, and I wasn't disturbed much while sleeping at night. The bathroom had a separate shower and toilet, and the bathtub was quite large. A common problem with Vietnamese hotels seems to be unstable water pressure and hot/cold water; mold was also clearly visible. The equipment looked high-quality in photos, but in actual use, it felt like cheap, knock-off items.


The first floor is the breakfast dining area. When we went downstairs the next day, it was probably still too early; the Vietnamese didn't feel hot, so they didn't turn on the air conditioning. They only turned it on around 8 am when it got a little warm. On the third day, it rained, and the weather was cooler, so they didn't turn on the air conditioning either. The dining environment was clean, and the selection was quite good, much better than the supposedly four-star sea-view hotel we stayed at in Da Nang later. This time, we chose the hotel's spa. Firstly, we didn't have to travel long distances, and secondly, it was more comfortable to shower before the massage. The price was reasonable. Although they asked if we wanted a strong, regular, or gentle massage, it felt like they were just asking. The gentle massage felt a bit painful, while my wife's strong massage felt too soft. There were welcome snacks before the massage, but the staff stood in front of us, making it impossible to relax. The bamboo tube spa really involved rolling heated bamboo tubes over our bodies—it was so hot it hurt! It's more suitable for people who like a strong massage and have thicker skin.


This accommodation included one free airport transfer from Da Nang to the hotel. You'll see staff holding nameplates as you exit the airport. If you book through the hotel, the transfer to Da Nang costs 300,000 VND. Previous reviews mentioned that calling a Grab car is cheaper, and the hotel's rental cars weren't in great condition. Considering the rainy season and the potential difficulty in finding a ride, I booked through the hotel beforehand. The car used was a manual Vios, and it was indeed quite old, but the driver was okay.

In terms of price, there are probably more affordable accommodations in Hoi An, but a river-view room for less than 2,000 VND per night for six days is acceptable. It's about a 15-minute walk to the Old Town and about a 10-minute walk to the Hoi An Show. However, if you have elderly people or children, staying in the Old Town would be more convenient.

The rooms are clean and the view is better than anywhere else in the area, but the hallway is like a greenhouse and very hot. They don't turn on the air conditioning in the hallway, only in the rooms. Lizards might come up onto the balcony in the evening, but they don't enter the rooms. Also, there are flying cockroaches, typical of Vietnam, in the hallway; they do enter the rooms, but the probability is low because the room air conditioning keeps the temperature low.

The breakfast is on the smaller side in terms of variety and size, but the taste is above average. The pho changes daily with options like beef and chicken. The bread is French-style, which has a different texture than German bread, but I am satisfied. On days when stir-fried chicken is served, you can make a top-notch chicken banh mi by dipping a baguette in it.

The shower water in the bathroom is clean.

From midnight to 10 AM, a chicken from the next-door neighbor crows; by around 10 AM, it crows so loudly that its voice becomes hoarse, and then it stops, perhaps because its voice is hoarse.

The remote control stopped working because the battery died; it would have been nice if they had provided spare batteries.

text:
Cozy An Boutique Hotel is a lovely, quaint property in a great location, about a 10 minute walk from Hoi An’s Old Town.

The location was perfect for us as it’s not too busy and we could stroll into the old town along the river or via the road. Near the hotel there are plenty of restaurants, spas, minimarts, coffee shops and a laundromat all within easy walking distance. There’s also a newly opened sports bar with the largest tv screen in Hoi An a few doors down serving AMAZING hot pies.

The hotel is beautifully decorated and has a good sized swimming pool, free bicycles and a buffet breakfast with a good variety of options. There is also a small gym, although we didn’t use it as there are only a few pieces of equipment. The rooms are a decent size, clean and have a nice view. As we’re travelling with kids, we opted for a family interconnecting room, which was well priced and adequate for what we needed.

I booked a room with a river view on the 7th floor and stayed for two nights.

The price was about 150,000 won for two nights.

I was also able to use the free pickup service from Da Nang, so I saved about 10,000 won on taxi fare.

Above all, the staff were incredibly friendly.

I was especially grateful for the local staff member who liked Korea and could speak a little Korean and treated me with such kindness.

The breakfast was fresh and delicious, and since it was served from 6:30 AM to 10:00 AM, I liked being able to enjoy a leisurely breakfast compared to other hotels.

The swimming pool next door was also well-maintained, and I made good use of the free bicycle rental service.

If you know how to ride a motorbike, I recommend renting one for about 1.5 million VND per day.

It is really convenient for getting around the area.

Overall, I was very satisfied with the value for money, and the staff were incredibly friendly.

If I come back to Hoi An, this is a place I definitely want to stay at again.
Thanks Huy and Jiju for a great stay! This hotel is clean and located very close to the ancient town, would recommend

text:
My first Vietnam trip = NAMIA. 🇻🇳✨

I originally chose Vietnam for this trip because I wanted to stay at InterContinental Danang. It was exactly my kind of hotel. But for just one night, I worried that the location might mean seeing very little beyond the resort.

Then I found Namia River Retreat — and choosing Namia completely changed the trip.

Our private villa came with its own pool, the food was fantastic, the farm-to-table concept was such a lovely touch, and the whole property had this incredibly peaceful atmosphere. 🌿

The breakfast was especially memorable. The bánh xèo was so crispy and delicious that we ordered it several times. In fact, everything we tried was so good that every meal became something to look forward to.

There were also so many activities and experiences to enjoy that we wished we had more time. We wanted to try everything, but our stay was simply too short. If we visit again, we would love to stay longer and fully enjoy everything Namia has to offer.

And one of the biggest perks? A 90-minute spa treatment is included in the stay. 🙌

Yes — 90 minutes. Included.

And this is not your typical hotel spa. I could write a whole separate review about it, but I’ll simply say:

Just go. Experience it for yourself. You’ll understand. 🤍

Then there was Tuyen.

We were celebrating a birthday, so this was already a special trip for us. From before we even arrived, Tuyen helped arrange our spa and sunset cruise, sent thoughtful reminders before our reservations, and our buggy was waiting for us before we even had to ask. 😂

Tuyen also arranged a river-view upgrade for us, and the view was absolutely beautiful. 🌅 For a one-night stay, that thoughtful gesture meant even more. It made our short stay feel incredibly special.

At one point, I actually thought:

“Wait… do we have a personal butler now?” 😂

That’s how attentive the service felt.

And then came the 4 PM late check-out.

For a one-night stay?!

FOUR. PM. 😭😂

I didn’t even know that was possible.

The Vietnamese afternoon heat had me a little nervous about spending the day outside, but the extra time meant we could slow down and enjoy our private pool, the river view, the spa, and simply do absolutely nothing.

And that is exactly what a retreat should feel like. 🤍

Beyond the beautiful villa, the food, and the facilities, it was the thoughtful hospitality that stayed with us.

Tuyen made our first Vietnam experience one we’ll always remember — not just as a beautiful stay, but as a very special birthday trip filled with moments we’ll treasure. ❤️

So now, when I think of Vietnam…

Vietnam = Namia.

If you’re looking for another typical five-star hotel, there are plenty of them.

But if you want a true retreat — private, peaceful, beautifully designed, with incredible food, a 90-minute spa included, plenty of activities, and service that feels genuinely personal — choose Namia.

Don’t overthink it.

Just go. You’ll understand. 🌿✨

And if Tuyen is your host, you’re in very good hands. 🤍

As a luxury travel advisor who spends a lot of time visiting and evaluating hotels around the world, Namia River Retreat really stood out to me during my time in Hoi An.

First, the food was out of this world. Every meal felt thoughtful, fresh, and beautifully prepared. I also loved the design of the accommodations. Having a private plunge pool with every room is such a great touch, and the complimentary bikes make it incredibly easy to explore the surrounding area. pro tip (vietnam breakfast via room service in the morning).

What really sets Namia apart for me is the wellness component. The included daily spa treatment is something I rarely see, and it became one of my favorite parts of the stay. The riverside sauna and cold plunge were equally fantastic and added to that feeling of truly being on a retreat.

text:
An unforgettable stay with exceptional hospitality! 🌴✨

We have just spent three incredible days at Rivertown Resort & Spa in Hoi An, and honestly, it has been one of the best hotel experiences of our lives!

From the moment we walked in, Mr. Tung made us feel incredibly welcome. He was absolutely amazing, taking the time to sit us down, explain everything and ensure we were comfortable. Within just 10 minutes of checking in, he had arranged an upgrade to a beautiful Riverfront King Room on a higher floor. As if that wasn’t already incredible, we were also treated to complimentary evening high tea, which was hands down one of the most luxurious, elegant and memorable experiences we have ever had. The attention to detail and generosity exceeded all our expectations.

We also booked our coconut basket boat experience through the hotel, and everything was organised seamlessly. Our driver picked us up directly from the hotel, and on the way back, when we asked if we could visit the pottery village, he happily dropped us off at no extra cost. These thoughtful gestures really show how much the team cares about its guests.

The resort itself is absolutely beautiful, with a tropical atmosphere, stunning river views and a lovely swimming pool that makes the whole place feel like a little paradise. With the river flowing alongside the property and beautiful views on both sides, it is such a peaceful and relaxing place to stay.

The buffet breakfast was another highlight. The selection was fantastic, and we enjoyed some of the best traditional Vietnamese food we have ever tasted. One particularly lovely touch was watching a lady handcrafting fresh Vietnamese rice paper rolls right there in the buffet area. Everything was delicious, and the quality of the food was exceptional.

Every staff member we encountered was warm, friendly and welcoming, but Mr. Tung deserves a very special mention. His kindness, professionalism, genuine hospitality and willingness to go above and beyond made our stay truly unforgettable. He made us feel valued and cared for, and he is an absolute credit to the resort.

We cannot thank the entire team enough for making our three days in Hoi An so special. It is rare to find a hotel where the facilities, food, atmosphere and hospitality are all this exceptional.

If you are visiting Hoi An, we wholeheartedly recommend Rivertown Resort & Spa! We would return in a heartbeat and would love to see Mr. Tung and the wonderful team again.

Thank you for making this such a beautiful and unforgettable experience. We will always remember our stay here! ❤️

text: Greetings from Malaysia. We were greeted by friendly staff when checking in, process was precise and did not waste too much time. Booked the studio room for a week and it was spacious and neat with ample space for 2 pax to move around and open our luggage. There's a bathtub in the toilet which is elevated and couples can enjoy a nice bath to unwind especially when it's hot outside. There's also a pool on the top floor if you fancy a swim, very intimate space and not for a big crowd but most of the time you should be able to have the space to yourself. Breakfast every morning was outstanding with complimentary drinks (if you opted for breakfast). Location wise it is fairly close to the beach (depending on how prime of the beach area you wanna be at) and very easy to get a Grab ride to everywhere in Da Nang. 24/7 convenience store is also situated several blocks away, very walkable. Overall stay was very pleasant, highly recommended if you want to escape the busyness of Da Nang main area (you'll be guaranteed to have quality sleep). Thank you Nikola, Lily, and the wonderful staff team (that I didn't manage to get their names) for the hospitality and meeting our requests promptly.

text:

The downsides were that swimming is only allowed until 6 PM, and I was surprised by how limited the breakfast selection was for a 5-star hotel.

I probably won't order breakfast next time I visit.

place: Hyatt Regency Danang Resort and Spa
text:
We had an amazing 6 nights at this property in a Regency Suite Club Room which was absolutely huge. The bath was amazing, the walk in wardrobe also and massive balcony.

We came to have a break of quiet relaxation and although being a huge resort with what appeared many families, we spent the days by the Regency Pool which meant we were generally the only people there. There is also an adults only pool which was a bit further away.

The Regency Club was fantastic for breakfast and evening drinks and canapés. Only suggestion would be to enforce a dress code to prevent people wandering around in thongs and very casual attire. Would also suggest making one end of the lounge more explicitly a ‘quiet zone’ or for adults only.

Xanh House had amazing food. Loved the Banh Mi!

Overall, we loved it here but the best part about this property are the staff. Every single person we encountered was just amazing. Special call outs to Doris in the lounge, Tuan Pham in Concierge and everyone else. I wish I could remember everyone’s names because you were fantastic!

Our one complaint and reason for not giving 5 stars is the ‘Little Farm’. No hotel should have a petting zoo. There were a couple of animals including a goat and a rabbit which looked very unwell. The rabbit could not walk and was lying in its own filth in the scorching sun. I would strongly suggest that this closes and is used just as a garden.

This property is definitely worth staying at. Even if just for the staff & service alone.

place: Hyatt Regency Danang Resort and Spa
trip_context: {"Trip type": "Vacation", "Travel group": "Solo", "Safety": "not safe", "Walkability": "terrible"}
text:
Beautiful grounds, but no place for a quiet stay

I stayed solo October 2026, on a points redemption. Hyatt markets this resort as sitting on "a tranquil stretch" of Non Nuoc beach. On the first day of my stay, a large private event in a tent within sight and earshot of my room ran a full concert production from 5 pm to 10 pm: hundreds of badge-wearing attendees, moving lights, concert-level sound, and multiple live singers and musicians. A letter handed to me at check-in mentioned an event and its setup, but no one explained it, nothing in it suggested a concert, and no quieter room was offered in advance. I was offered a move only after the music started, when I was already sick in bed.

I was ill for much of the stay and had to arrange my own doctor through personal contacts. No one at the resort offered medical help. Other lapses: I was sent down the entrance ramp in heavy rain to collect a Grab delivery of medicine, the check-in sheet listed the wrong room service hours, my final breakfast order was wrong, and there was a dead bird outside my room (photo attached), a faulty fan switch, confusing light switches, and broken lights.

Update: Management apologized in writing and in person, covered some room charges. They declined to refund any of the points I redeemed and offered 15,000 bonus points instead. Housekeeping was excellent, and the front office manager was gracious, but I won't return. Families with young kids may enjoy the pools and kids' club. Solo travelers and couples looking for quiet should look elsewhere, or at least ask at check-in whether any events are scheduled.

text: Hoi An Resort is a luxurious and excellent resort that has it all, featuring a variety of rooms and facilities, a golf course, and a casino. It truly deserves a 5-star rating. I think I have visited about 5 or 6 times. The Residences, New World Hotel, and the higher-class Beach Resort and Suite Resort are all great options for families (I have stayed in every room type); there is almost no difference in quality between them. The Beach and Suite Resorts, which are attached to the casino, are simply a bit more upscale and offer better accessibility. You can get around by buggy or walk for 5 minutes. Hoi An Shores Golf Course is a links course that is well-maintained. I have visited every golf course in Da Nang, and the management here is top-notch (personally, I like dunes and links courses). With Vinpearl Golf Course just 5 minutes away, it is ideal for a golf trip. It is also close to Hoi An Old Town, so there are plenty of things to eat, see, and enjoy, such as massages, dining, and performances. You can even take a basket boat ride at the mouth of the Thu Bon River. Thanks to the shuttle service, the convenience and accessibility for traveling between Hoi An, Da Nang, and the airport are excellent. The staff are all friendly and kind, and the service is truly top-notch. It is a service that accommodates everything. The breakfast is delicious, and there is a wide variety of food. All the facilities are spacious and luxurious. There is a food court called "Garden" that features Vietnamese, Chinese, and Korean cuisine, including the restaurant *Obaltan*. There are two swimming pools, a cafe with an infinity pool, and a dry sauna next to it (free of charge). And the highlight of this resort is, of course, the casino. It is the best resort because it allows for a hotel staycation, golf, casino, and sightseeing all at once.

I would like to start this review by highlighting that this is clearly an ownership/maintenance issue and NOT the fault of the lovely staff who were willing to attempt to sort out these issues that are out of their control.

Unfortunately, myself and my partner had a negative experience staying at HA Ocean Front, and I honestly don’t understand how there aren’t more reviews of people experiencing the same issues.

Firstly, when we initially arrived, we noticed that the front foyer and lobby was quite cluttered and untidy. Not an immediate issue, and it was at night time so we thought that perhaps our judgement was clouded. However, as we were walking up to our room we noticed a lot of stains on the carpets and walls, holes in carpet, and in front of the elevator, a couple of dead cockroaches. This is when we were becoming more uncomfortable of the cleanliness of the hotel.

After we were shown our room by their lovely night shift staff, we immediately noticed that the room was not up to standard as per shown on the photos. The floors were dusty and dirty, the roof was mouldy looking, the aircon wasn’t working properly, but worst of all, was the bathroom. The bathroom was just downright disgusting. The tiles in the bathroom and shower were cracked, mouldy, and clearly had not been cleaned properly due to a lack of maintenance. There was no toilet roll holder for the toilet paper, and there was a hole in the wall that had been badly patched up that we assume was from the old toilet roll holder. Our sink was clean to the naked eye, however there was a crusty lump of god knows what stuck to the side of the sink that resembled a booger or something of the sort.

The next morning, we spoke to the reception lady who did her best to ensure our comfortability was prioritised (offered us a new room, an upgrade at no cost) but ultimately, my partner and I decided it was best to checkout immediately as we did not feel comfortable staying at the hotel under the current conditions.

Again, this is no direct fault of the staff who simply work there and try their best to ensure their guests have an enjoyable stay, but this fell really flat for us. On booking.com they are listed as a 4 star hotel with a score of 8.4, but I truly do not understand how, when the hotel is presented in such a state, and there seems to be a lack of people experiencing the same issues. Hopefully, the business can reflect on this review and these issues, as they do have the potential, but it is clearly an ownership and maintenance issue.

place: Le Domaine De Tam Hai Resort
text: An extraordinary few days here. We came across this place via the Vietnam Coracle and booked three nights through Facebook. We arrived via the ferry north of the mainland (5k each), it is a short 5 min walk to the resort once you arrive. The resort has changed somewhat to described in the 2019 article we read, I would think Covid and some flooding events have impacted. In mid April, we had the resort to ourselves bar another couple arriving the morning we left. The resort holds incredible charm, the villas are clean, the seperate open bathroom area is an experience in itself. Do not come for luxury here, you will share the resort with plenty of wildlife (villa aside) ants, lizards, mozies, cicadas etc. Vy, who runs the place, was brilliant. Breakfast is included, if you want to have lunch and dinner there you order in the morning so she can have it delivered from the market and prepare. Kayaks are still there and free, and Vy had bicycles for us for day two and three of our stay - these are essential to go explore the island which is an easy cycle, 6km long and 4km wide, go explore and meet the wonderful friendly locals, maybe have lunch out. Otherwise your food will be at the resort and it is good. After dark though you'll essentially be back to your villa (which didn't have WiFi) so bring a good book or have download something at the bar area which does have good WiFi. This place is off the track, we had it to ourselves and in fact were the only foreigners on the island having cycled around it two days. Pool, sun, quiet relaxation, perfect. Would love to have seen this place in 2019 but delighted to have experienced it in 2026 and hope it continues to thrives and attract independent travellers looking for the above. Thank you Vy.

We spend one week at Le Domaine and loved every minute of it!
If you’d like peace and quiet and an island which is a wonderful of the beaten track experience then this is the place for you!
The huts are cosy and clean, the beds comfy! The swimming pool great and you can spend your days fishing, take a boat trip to a beautiful coralreef or cycle the island and experience the local life of Vietnam.
Another plus of this resort is the amazing chef and the kind and super helpful host. They both will try their best to help you with anything!
Sure some parts of the resort could do with a little upgrade: for instance the poolside furniture, the soccer table and the outside of the huts on the far side. The pool table died all together. But in no way that influenced our experience.
The staff is amazing and if we can we will definitely come back!

This hotel now takes the top spot as my absolute favorite hotel of all time!

Even though it was the rainy season, we were blessed with surprisingly wonderful weather. Getting a great rate combined with fewer tourists made every single experience and activity feel like an extra upgrade.

What impressed me most is that the activities and experiences here are so rich that anyone can find exactly what they’re looking for. You can come to indulge in delicious cuisine, play at a golf course ranked among Asia’s Top 100, enjoy yoga, water sports, and pickleball, or explore their incredible facilities: 4 swimming pools (including stunning infinity pools), a relaxing private beach, multiple spa options, a casino, and an entertainment hall.

Foodies will be amazed by over 20 restaurants featuring international cuisines from all around the world—our personal favorites are Blend and QNH! On top of all that, they provide convenient free shuttle services to and from the airport, as well as to the nearby Hoi An Ancient Town. You will easily find one reason to visit, and a million reasons never to leave.

First of all, a heartfelt thank you to the front desk team who welcomed our three parties. On top of walking us through all the hotel facilities and details, they also recommended plenty of fun activities and great local restaurants, allowing us to plan our itinerary seamlessly.

Special thanks as well to the QNH restaurant team—a gentleman with glasses and a lady who speaks Chinese. Both were incredibly friendly and made us feel right at home.

Finally, thank you to Nick and Chelsea (?) for assisting us with checkout. All of these made our stay truly unforgettable, and we will definitely be coming back again!

text:
Hoiana Beach Resort Hotel is one of three accommodation options on the same premises, which can make the layout and facilities a little confusing at first. However, it feels noticeably more luxurious than the other two hotels in the complex.

The lobby is clean and pleasant, with a nice fresh smell. This is a significant contrast to the casino-side lobby next door, which had a strong cigarette smell. The reception staff spoke good English and made the check-in process smooth.

The room was new, spacious, spotless, and close to perfect. Housekeeping did an amazing job throughout our stay. The pillows were on the softer side, so guests who prefer firmer support may find them less comfortable. The hallways outside the rooms were also somewhat warm and humid.

I liked the hotel’s location. It is a shorter ride to Hoi An, which was the main area we wanted to visit. The hotel operates a shuttle service to Hoi An, although the logistics and schedule were a little confusing, we still managed to catch the shuttle without too much trouble.

Breakfast was also excellent, with a good overall selection and quality, though I think the spread (should) can increase a bit if more guests are staying.

Overall, Hoiana Beach Resort Hotel offers a comfortable stay and convenient for visiting Hoi An without the chaotic in the older part of the old town. Recommend 👍🏻

text:
A truly special Robinson Club – absolutely perfect! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

I stayed at the Robinson Club Vietnam with my daughter, and we were both incredibly happy! The expansive grounds are beautifully maintained, the atmosphere is tranquil yet vibrant.

I'd especially like to highlight the fitness classes – the level is truly top-notch. The outdoor platform overlooking the sea is a dream and makes every workout an experience.

The rooms are spacious, the bathrooms roomy, and even the hairdryer works perfectly – which isn't always the case 😉. All the staff are incredibly friendly, service-oriented, and dedicated. The Vietnamese are such a warm and welcoming people – you can feel it in every interaction.

The food was delicious and varied, the evening shows were spectacular – the dancers really gave it their all! I've never experienced a club where the presence of the club director was so noticeable – you were greeted and seen off almost personally. It creates a truly special atmosphere.

The surrounding area is also beautiful – it's worth exploring the nearby towns. A little heads-up: the rainy season starts in mid-October. We had a few showers, but it stayed warm, and you experience nature in a truly impressive way.

My daughter made some wonderful friends, and the pools are perfect for playing and relaxing.

In short: a thoroughly enjoyable holiday that I can wholeheartedly recommend. I've stayed at many Robinson Clubs, but this one is truly something special.

P.S. I almost forgot about the beach! It's absolutely unique! I've never seen or experienced anything like it before!

text:
Disappointing pre-holiday experience.

First, there was discriminatory treatment at check-in. No one greeted us in the lobby; we had to go to the reception desk ourselves. It's unclear if the difference in service was due to the room type or something else, but the guests at the next table received welcome drinks first, had staff check them in at their table, and were even given a trolley to their room. I stared blankly for a while before the welcome drinks were finally served to my table.

Second, the soundproofing was poor. I booked a Tropical Deluxe room on the lower floor, and the children running around downstairs made a terrible racket that made it impossible to rest until late at night. I had to call reception twice to ask them to turn the noise down, and I'm not sure if they helped. One person was sick and wanted to rest, the other wanted a quiet space to work. Neither of us got what we wanted, and we were annoyed until almost midnight when the noise finally stopped.

And the customer service was poor. At check-out, the receptionist asked about the poor soundproofing in the room last night, but apologized and said they hoped for a better experience next time. With such a bad experience after just one night, who would dare stay a second time with you?!

Breakfast was quite basic, probably because I had high expectations for the resort. Its location is far from the city center; I thought it would be quiet, but the soundproofing was terrible. It's not worth going to this remote area and staying here for the purpose of relaxation.

I will not return and would not recommend staying here.

text:
MI CASA BEACHFRONT – A PEACEFUL SPACE IN TAM THANH
I visited Mi Casa Beachfront in Tam Thanh on a sunny day in early September, with a blue sea and gentle waves. It was a very pleasant place – unpretentious, quiet, intimate, and peaceful.
Located in the heart of Tam Thanh Mural Village, Mi Casa boasts a lush green space with many trees, bougainvillea, and numerous beautiful photo spots. Especially noteworthy is its beachfront location; just a few steps away is the wide, airy, and tranquil beach.
Our group had a wonderful time. Playing music on the second-floor lobby was fantastic, and we enjoyed strolling along the beach, watching the sunrise and sunset, and wandering through the Mural Village.

It's raining in Hanoi and I suddenly missed Mi Casa so much that I had to write a review right away! 🥹
My family had an extremely satisfying experience here.
The owner and the housekeeper were incredibly friendly. After staying here, I just want to leave the city and go to the beach!

The homestay is bright, beautiful, and well-equipped. It has a kitchen, laundry facilities, and a patio for barbecues and hot pot. The beach is just a short walk away. The sandy beach is long, smooth, and gently sloping. The water is crystal clear; you can see the sand clearly when you dive. The beach is uncrowded. You might encounter fishermen pulling in their nets and women gathering clams from early morning until noon. In the early morning, opening your room door will immediately reveal the fresh air mixed with the scent of the sea – simply wonderful.

Thank you so much, Hanh and your family, for choosing and staying 3 nights at Mi Casa for the September 2nd holiday and for your satisfaction at our home – your home :).

Wishing your family good health, peace, and happiness!

Staying at Mi Casa this season was a amazing experience! Quang Nam in this period is famous for its fierce hot and dry wind, strong sunshine, and salty ocean air – a true Central Vietnam vibe. But don't worry, the house is surprisingly cool, super clean, and very comfortable inside, making it the perfect place to relax after exploring.

I had a great holiday at Mi Casa!
This place is very peaceful and not too noisy like other tourist areas. The beach has long golden sand, and you can watch local fishermen working every day. In the morning, I went to the fish market to wait for the boats coming back and bought fresh fish to cook by myself.

The house is super clean and has everything comfortable just like my own home. I slept very well with the sound of ocean waves. Especially, the host is super friendly and gave very clear and detailed instructions. I really love this place!

text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ **A place well worth escaping from the hustle and bustle of city life**

Mi Casa Beachfront left me with a very pleasant feeling – not overly fancy, not noisy, but truly intimate and peaceful.

Located in the tranquil Tam Thanh Mural Village, Mi Casa Beachfront boasts a unique atmosphere: lush greenery, abundant trees, vibrant bougainvillea, and many "chill" corners. From the characteristic green walls, the art paintings in the rooms, the bougainvillea trellis in front of the house, to the courtyard overlooking the sea, and the BTNT road from Mrs. Mai's house to the seawall – every corner has its own charm, perfect for taking photos. 🌿🌸🌊

What I liked most was its prime beachfront location; just stepping out of the house allows you to enjoy a very private beach experience. The beach is wide, spacious, and quite peaceful. The feeling of being immersed in the water, watching the sunrise or sunset, is an unforgettable sense of tranquility.

Our group had a wonderful time: taking photos together, strolling along the beach, watching the sunset, and sitting together chatting and singing in a very peaceful atmosphere.

If you're looking for a private, quiet beachfront spot suitable for a group of friends/family, I think Mi Casa Beachfront is a very worthwhile option. It's a place that doesn't need too much activity; just being there makes you feel… a little slower and much more relaxed. 💙

text:
My family and I are staying just two nights at the beachfront villas. The resort is grand, carefully designed, and well kept; the gardeners and cleaners deserve credit for maintaining such high standards.

My villa includes a butler, and I want to commend Thuỷ, who made this brief visit pleasant and restful. She anticipated and prepared every request. The space is generous, with a separate living area and a bedroom in another structure. The bed is comfortable and the pillows are soft. Amenities are top quality. The mini-bar is not inclusive in cost of stay like other luxury resorts, but it provides a tasty pre-mixed negroni bottle each day. Housekeeping is excellent at keeping the room clean. The in-villa pool is small but enjoyable, while the public pool is huge.

I appreciate that bicycles are available for every villa. Cycling to breakfast or the spa feels quicker and simpler.

The spa is serene and attractive, with high-quality products. Still, my treatment did not meet expectations. My masseur tried to adjust to my requests, yet her skill did not match the cost.

Breakfast offers many options but feels chaotic. The restaurant staff seem to need more training; they focus more on foreign tables than local ones. For two days in a row, our orders were forgotten or mixed up. While we sat outside, cushions were not provided until I asked.

In short, my stay was enjoyable because of Thuỷ’s efforts. Thank you again, Thuỷ.

place: Four Seasons Resort The Nam Hai, Hoi An
text:
An Exceptional Stay — One of the Best Family Experiences We’ve Had

We spent three wonderful nights at Four Seasons Resort The Nam Hai, and what truly sets this hotel apart is its exceptional level of service and genuine attention to detail.

From the moment we arrived, we felt incredibly welcomed and cared for. The staff have a remarkable ability to notice and remember individual preferences, anticipate needs, and make every guest feel genuinely special. It is not simply excellent service — it is thoughtful, personal hospitality that makes the entire experience feel effortless.

Travelling with two young children, aged one and five, I was particularly impressed by how beautifully the resort caters to families. Our villa was prepared with so many thoughtful little touches: adorable children’s bathrobes and slippers in the right sizes, books, toys, and lovely little surprises and treats for the girls.

What impressed me even more were the practical details. Even something as simple as a small step stool in the bathroom, allowing a child to reach the sink independently, shows just how carefully the resort has considered the needs of its youngest guests. These may seem like minor things, but as a parent, they make an enormous difference. You can tell that welcoming children here is not an afterthought — it is genuinely part of the resort’s philosophy.

A very special mention goes to the Kids Club, which is easily one of the best we have experienced.

Although the indoor space is relatively compact, it is beautifully designed, with huge windows, an abundance of natural light, and a wonderful variety of activities. Rather than feeling like an enclosed playroom, it feels bright, welcoming, and connected to the outdoors.

What I appreciated most was the flexibility and personal attention. There is a daily activity schedule, but the staff are wonderfully accommodating to each child’s interests. If your child doesn’t feel like making bracelets, they can make lanterns instead. If lanterns aren’t appealing either, there is always another creative activity to explore. Nothing feels rigid or forced.

The layout is absolutely brilliant for families. Right beside the indoor Kids Club is a shallow children’s pool, filled with pool toys, floats, water guns, and everything little ones could wish for. Just next to it is a large, shaded sandpit where children can build sandcastles and play comfortably out of the direct sun.

Children can move effortlessly between swimming, sand play, and indoor activities, all within the same dedicated area. With a toddler and a five-year-old, I found this setup almost perfect. Both children had plenty to enjoy, and the entire experience was wonderfully relaxed.

The beach deserves a special mention as well. It is absolutely beautiful — vast, immaculately clean, and incredibly peaceful. Whether taking a long walk along the shore, dipping your feet into the water, or simply enjoying the surroundings, it is a pleasure to be there. Despite the resort welcoming other guests, there is an extraordinary sense of space and privacy. You rarely feel surrounded by people.

What stays with me most, however, is the kindness and attentiveness of the people working here. It is the combination of genuine warmth, impeccable service, and countless thoughtful details that makes this resort so special.

Still giving 5 🌟 despite ranking location as 3 🌟 as a 4.5 🌟 aggregate isn't available as an option and the atmosphere and service more than offset the need to Scooter or Grab like 25KM to get anywhere of use other than Old Town. Speaking of, while the 1st Shuttle is at 12:15 (?) the free shuttle to and from OT is a very nice perk.

I am Titanium Elite and Lifetime Silver at the conclusion of this stay. So YMMV in terms of perks and upgrades. We got upgraded to a seafront facing Jr Suite which was just massive and likely a hair larger than our 2 Bedder in Saigon. Room was totally on point and up to Bonvoy standards, but there were some small quirks with the Housekeeping. Nothing worth detailing, just odd based on my experiences across over 30 Bonvoy properties in at least 5 countries.

Speaking of that knowledge / experience base, thr Brekkie here is decidedly the best I have ever seen at a Bonvoy. Just MASSIVE selection. Sushi, Sirloin tips, Banh Mi station, Vietnamese Coffee station abive the usual machine made Lattes, real Bacon 🥓 (I'm looking at you Renaissance Dhaka and Chennai), Brie and meats for making better than butter toast, and of course a proper made to order Ommelete. Seafront view with the only downside being some heavy sunlight if you come late and have to eat a non-shade table to secure the view.

Large tub in the room. Just a MASSIVE bed (see pic of the Fiancé for size reference...if you can even find her in the pic like a game of "Where's Waldo?"). Nice little **** couch and a large patio area for some relaxing Cuban smoke while listening to the Surf break. Especially at sunrise.

The Game Room with the Street Fighter arcade game and 8' Billiards table are a really cool touch, especially given the Fiancé's and my proclivity for that past time. The Hammocks are a really nice little perk, especially after one drink from Petit Kang in OT puts her straight on her 47KG butt for the rest of the afternoon.

Would definitely stay again. Massive value for the cash outlay or the points burned.

All staff treat you like Royalty, but again, at ~400 nights on my dossier with Bonvoy, YMMV.

Positioned just across the bridge from Hoi An’s Old Town, Moire offers convenient access to major sights while remaining removed from the immediate noise.

Rooms are modern and comfortable, while breakfast provides well-portioned dishes served on warmed plates. Driver Michael provided a great transfer in a luxury Mercedes SUV, and Mimy at the Yellow Bicycle restaurant was exceptionally warm and welcoming, they were truly the only two staff members we genuinely liked and appreciated during our stay.

Regrettably, the hotel struggled with basic housekeeping, communication, service anticipation, and hospitality grace.

Although modern, our room was noticeably dirty in several spots (see attached picture), and throughout our two-night stay, dirty dishes were left uncollected in the hallway corridor for the entire duration of our visit.

Upon landing in Danang, being exhausted, we inadvertently forgot about our booked transfer and arranged a Grab; however, for a 5-star luxury hotel that had our flight number and WhatsApp contact, we expected a proactive call or heads-up upon landing rather than a message two hours later while we were already en route. Although we profusely apologized via chat and willingly paid for the transfer anyway, the lobby and check-in staff repeatedly brought up and dwelled on how long the driver had been waiting, making us feel unnecessarily guilty throughout the check-in process.

Furthermore, during a sudden rainstorm at the pool, staff ran for shelter holding umbrellas over themselves without offering assistance or umbrellas to guests trying to cover their belongings (see attached picture).

Lastly, the breakfast setup requires guests to walk to a booth just to order eggs that are later delivered to the table, and takeaway coffee is strictly prohibited, which felt unnecessarily restrictive for a boutique property.

text:
We stayed at Moire Hoi An for one night in a garden-view room, and it ended up being one of the best hotel experiences of our Vietnam trip.

From check-in, the staff made us feel very welcome. The welcome drink was delicious, and although the main lobby was under renovation, the hotel arranged a golf cart to take us to the check-in area, which made everything very smooth.

Our room was exceptionally clean, modern and beautifully designed. The fresh flowers on the table were such a nice touch and immediately made the room feel more special. The minibar was well stocked, the bathtub was large, and we also loved the hotel’s yellow colonial-style architecture.

What really made this stay memorable, though, was the staff. Harry was incredibly warm and helpful. He shared many recommendations about Hoi An, local food, Vietnamese coffee and Vietnamese culture, and talking with him added so much to our trip.

We also joined the hotel’s lantern boat activity in the evening. The bartender working on September 15 was wonderful. He made excellent cocktails, helped us take many beautiful photos, and spent time chatting with us during the boat ride. Since no other guests joined that evening, it almost felt like we had a private boat experience, and it became one of our favorite memories from Hoi An.

We also joined the complimentary Vietnamese coffee experience, which was both fun and interesting. It was a nice way to learn more about Vietnamese coffee culture and made the stay feel even more special. A big thank you as well to the staff member who led the activity on September 15 — we really enjoyed the experience and appreciated the warm and engaging introduction.

Breakfast by the river was also excellent. The view and atmosphere were beautiful, the food was delicious, and we especially enjoyed the freshly made salt coffee. The hotel also provides complimentary bicycles, and riding through the streets of Hoi An was a great experience.

The only downside was that construction noise outside our room was quite noticeable.

It would also be great if the hotel could offer more transportation options in the future, such as shuttle services to places like the coconut village or the beach.

Overall, the staff at Moire made our stay feel genuinely special. Their kindness, professionalism and willingness to share local culture made our Vietnam trip even better. We would absolutely stay here again.

text:
Summary – (5/5) Excellent 4-night stay at the Moire Hoi An, a hotel that feels intimate but manages to maintain the professional feel of a true 5* property.

Group – 1 Family, 4 Adults, 1 x 2 yr old & 1 x 10-month-old, divided into 1 pool villa and 1 premium room.

Pre Arrival – (5/5)
This was a last-minute booking while escaping from another hotel, we had requested early check-in as front desk got in touch via whatsapp before arrival.

Check In - (5/5)
Early check-in was granted on the Premium room with the Villa being ready shortly after, both rooms were available before standard 3pm time which was much appreciated with 2 small children.

Villa - (5/5)
Spotless, modern, well maintained and looked after. Very good use of space for storage to keep the living spaces uncluttered. All amenities feel as a 5* should. The private pool & garden create a very nice contrast to the hustle and bustle of Hoi An old town and a place to relax and watch the lantern boats go by at night.

Service – (5/5)
With 2 small children we did quite a lot of in room dining, everything was delivered and cleared very promptly. Front desk would answer whatsapp questions or help with external bookings very efficiently. Everyone was genuinely helpful and conducted their duties with care and professionalism.

Food – (4.5/5)
The Vietnamese food was very good on par if not better than most restaurants we tried in the old town. The French food from Julienne restaurant was unfortunately not as good, not bad, but it did not live up to the same sort of expectations as the rest of the services in the hotel did. I suspect this is lack of regular use and chef experience; most people don’t come to Hoi An to eat French food.

Further Notes
• The prices of food, services and amenities are very competitive, my family dinners at the Vietnamese restaurant were comparable in price to higher tier local restaurants in town. Extra services such as airport transfer were also decently priced.
• Hotel grounds are exceptionally maintained.
• Free of charge bicycles also with child seat are a very nice touch.

text:
I am a resident of Hoi An and a regular guest who frequently enjoys the dining and other experiences at Almanity Hoi An. Because of this, I have always had a positive impression of the hotel and highly appreciated the quality of its services and hospitality.

However, I was genuinely disappointed by an incident that occurred yesterday at Four Plates Restaurant.

Yesterday, while I happened to be passing by the hotel and was in a hurry to attend to some urgent work, I suddenly needed to use the restroom. As I was in a rush, I entered the Four Plates Restaurant area and politely asked a staff member where the restroom was and whether I could use it. The staff member directed me to the restroom, and I followed the instructions accordingly.

However, after I finished using the restroom and was just walking out, the same staff member stopped me and informed me that, because I was not using any services at the restaurant, I was not allowed to use the restroom.

What surprised me even more was that I later realized this person was actually the restaurant manager.

I completely understand that the restaurant may have its own policies regarding the use of its facilities. However, if there is a policy stating that guests who are not dining at the restaurant are not permitted to use the restroom, I believe this could have been communicated to me from the beginning, before I used it. Having the staff direct me to the restroom and then stop me afterward to explain the policy made me feel very uncomfortable.

What disappointed me most was the way the manager communicated with me. I was even “instructed” on how I should speak or ask for permission if I wanted to enter the restaurant in the future. I genuinely do not understand why such a simple situation needed to be handled in a way that made me feel as though I had done something wrong.

I never intended to use any of the restaurant’s services without permission. From the very beginning, I specifically asked the staff member for permission before using the restroom. I also fully respect the rules and policies of both the hotel and the restaurant.

Therefore, what disappointed me was not simply whether I was allowed to use the restroom, but the way I was treated afterward. Being stopped by a restaurant manager and spoken to in a manner that made me feel as though I had done something inappropriate is something I genuinely did not expect from a five-star hotel.

I am not a tourist who simply happened to walk into Almanity. I live in Hoi An and am a regular guest who frequently uses the dining and other services at the hotel. Having had many positive experiences at Almanity, I find it even more disappointing that such a minor situation, which could easily have been handled with a simple and courteous explanation, instead left me feeling disrespected.

I sincerely hope that the Management Team will review this incident, particularly the way the situation was communicated and handled by the restaurant manager. I hope similar situations in the future can be handled in a more professional, thoughtful, and respectful manner, in line with the service standards that Almanity Hoi An aims to uphold.

I am sharing this feedback not because of a minor issue regarding the use of a restroom, but because I genuinely value my relationship with Almanity and care about the experience I receive as a regular guest. I hope that all guests, especially returning guests who regularly support the hotel, can always feel respected and treated with appropriate courtesy.
owner_reply:
Dear Mr. / Mrs. Jeanny Law,
Thank you for sharing your feedback with us. As a returning guest who has supported Almanity on many occasions, your experience and comments are particularly meaningful to us.
We are genuinely sorry that this interaction left you feeling uncomfortable and disrespected. We have reviewed the incident with our team and understand that, although there was a misunderstanding regarding the use of the restaurant's facilities, the communication could and should have been handled more thoughtfully.
Our facilities are primarily provided for hotel guests and customers using our services. At the same time, we understand that someone passing by may occasionally have an urgent need to use a restroom. In such situations, our team should communicate the arrangement clearly and courteously from the outset, rather than allowing a misunderstanding to arise afterward.
We have therefore taken your feedback on board and will reinforce with our managers and colleagues that how we communicate a policy is just as important as the policy itself. A simple operational matter should never make a guest feel unwelcome or embarrassed.
We sincerely appreciate your continued support of Almanity and the fact that you took the time to tell us how this experience made you feel. We hope to have the opportunity to welcome you back and provide you with the warm, thoughtful hospitality that you have experienced from us on previous visits.
Warm regards,
Phuong Le
Director of Operations

text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

A beautiful, authentic Vietnamese homestay that truly feels like home ❤️

I honestly cannot recommend Tan Doan An Bang Homestay highly enough. Tan and his beautiful Vietnamese family have a wonderful way of making you feel like part of their home.

The homestay itself is beautiful, clean, comfortable and incredibly well priced. The rooms are huge, with a lovely comfortable bed, a big TV, a spacious bathroom and plenty of storage for your clothes and belongings. There is a separate entry for guests and the pool is wonderful.

The location is also perfect, tucked away down a little quiet alley off the main street. You’re close to all the restaurants, cafés and everything A Bang has to offer, while still having peace and quiet. From the other side of the homestay, it’s just a short walk down the alley to the beach. You really couldn’t ask for a better location.

What makes this place so special is the family. Each morning I’ve been offered fresh fruit and coffee. I’ve been unwell during my stay and Linh has been incredibly caring and thoughtful by making me warm ginger drinks and looked after me when I wasn’t feeling well. That kindness and genuine care has meant so much to me. Thank you so much, Tan, Linh and your beautiful family, for welcoming me into your home and making me feel so cared for. ❤️

If you’re looking for somewhere authentic, peaceful, comfortable, affordable and genuinely welcoming while staying at An Bang Beach, this is the place to stay. 🇻🇳❤️

trip_context: {"Trip type": "Vacation", "Travel group": "Couple", "Hotel highlights": "Quiet"}
text:
We booked a room at the last minute while staying in Hoi An. Mai, Nhan and Loi at reception (and Thung in the restaurant) made the process easy and straightforward, and were extremely gracious and understanding when we faced some external difficulties at the end of our stay. We can’t thank them enough for helping us to have the best possible experience under tricky circumstances.

If you want to be near the action, but not right in it, this is the place for you. It is situated just south of the very busy An Bang Beach area, a short ride on a free push bike. The street is a little quieter and away from the hustle of tourists, but hosts a couple of amazing live music venues just across the road and some fantastic restaurants in the resort, and just down the street.

The resort has excellent views of the Cham Islands, and a lovely natural setting between the rooms and the beach, with bespoke swings, seating areas and lounges that are fun and relaxing. A choice of 3 pools is also a bonus. (At this time the beach is under construction due to a natural disaster late last year, however this didn’t impact on our stay too much)

We had a really lovely stay here, and wouldn’t hesitate to return.

Thanks again to the wonderful staff here! 🥰

text: I had an amazing stay at this hotel! The room was beautiful, spacious, and very clean. The staff were incredibly kind, friendly and helpful. They made me feel very welcome and well taken care of. I would definitely recommend this hotel to everyone. It is honestly one of the best hotels I have ever stayed at. I would love to come back again! Aira boutique is number one!👍👍

It is right in front of An Bang Beach, and the room condition is good. The balcony is a bit small for sitting and drinking a beer. The breakfast has limited options, but each item is delicious. I think you shouldn't expect much from the swimming pool; it was smaller than I thought. Perhaps because An Bang Beach itself is quiet, it seems perfect for a peaceful rest without any noise at all.

I would love to come back to Aira Hotel, located right next to An Bang Beach.

Compared to Da Nang city center or Hoi An Old Town, this area is much quieter, and you can really feel the peaceful and authentic charm of a small seaside village. The staff were also incredibly kind and welcoming.

From check-in to breakfast and check-out, they took great care of us with thoughtful attention to detail. They also checked our schedule and kindly helped us whenever needed.

The room was beautiful, the bedding was very comfortable, and although the pool was not very large, it was 1.4 meters deep, which made it perfect for enjoying a proper swim.

If you are looking for the relaxed atmosphere of An Bang Beach and genuinely kind people, I highly recommend staying here.

Cua Dai Beach is generally quite nice. The sea is clean during peak season. There's not much trash. There are almost no stray snorkels🐕. Jellyfish🪼 and other biting sea creatures are also almost nonexistent. The bottom is smooth and sandy. A breakwater has been cleverly constructed near the shore, effectively dampening the waves. There are no tricky or treacherous currents in the water, but it's still not recommended to swim too far out...🏊‍♀️
There are almost no ships, no annoying boats, parachutes, or other activities. The views along the shore🌴 are beautiful. Da Nang is visible in the distance. Occasionally, construction occurs along the shore, shoreline reinforcement is done, or previously started hotels are being built.
You can stroll along the shore. There are small cafes serving cocktails and cold 🍻 beer.
There are quite a few picturesque abandoned and unfinished hotels. Looking at them, you think how fleeting everything is... 🤷‍♀️
There aren't many tourists. There are 🏨 hotels nearby, like the Wyndham, Coy, Victoria, Marriott, Alli, and others. But due to the exorbitant prices, people come for 1-2 days and quickly leave...
And, of course, there are crazy bloggers who are probably already asleep hugging their phones, filming everything, but that's rather rare...which is good news)))😄😄

We were shocked when we reached this beach. The colorful heart with the inscription "Cua Dai Beach" seems almost cynical given the devastating state of the surroundings. The beach has been completely destroyed and is unusable due to massive construction work. Excavators, construction vehicles, and torn-up sand are everywhere. But the worst thing is the atmosphere. Many buildings along the beach appear completely abandoned and dilapidated. You can't help but be reminded of a horror or zombie movie. I wanted to stay in a local accommodation rather than a hotel or resort, so I made a reservation and found An Bang Beach Villa La. Honestly, the staff are very friendly.

However, the facilities show signs of age.

Although it is kept clean,

I would not recommend it for a couples' trip.

It seems like it wouldn't be bad for a trip with friends or family.

text:
Checked in on August 7, 2026.

We booked two triple rooms and two double rooms.

The cleanliness and comfort were consistently praised by our family.

The location is situated within Hoi An's night market.

You can easily go shopping downstairs, and if you get tired, it's just a short walk back to your room to rest. The price is also very reasonable, making it a great value.

Upon check-in, the front desk staff provides a small map highlighting nearby attractions and shops, as well as information on possible sightseeing activities in Hoi An.

The hot water pressure was good, and the room air conditioning was quite cool. Beer, cola, snacks, and instant noodles are available in the room for a fee, so please be aware of this upon check-in.

While the breakfast isn't comparable to a four- or five-star resort, it's still a very good option.

Additionally, a paid airport transfer service is offered. The cost is announced upon booking. The price isn't expensive, and the car was very clean, the driving was smooth and comfortable, unlike the drivers we encountered in Vietnam a few days ago who kept honking their horns. 😆

text:
This is a truly fantastic, amazing, and beautiful hotel. The French-style interior features detailed decor, and the color scheme and furniture in each room are unique. The attention to detail is meticulously crafted down to the smallest aspects. It is very charming. The staff are very friendly and well-trained. Although I have stayed at other 5-star and boutique hotels, this one left such a strong impression that it perfectly matched my taste. I would recommend this to honeymooners looking for a place that isn't just a big, flashy, and crowded hotel. A hotel I definitely want to stay at again... This hotel is absolutely fantastic—beautiful, charming, and honestly, a little dangerous… because once you stay here, ordinary hotels may never feel quite the same again!

The entire hotel feels like a carefully designed French-style boutique dream. Every room has its own personality, with a completely different layout, color palette, furniture, and little details. Nothing feels mass-produced or copied and pasted from a hotel catalog. You can tell that someone put an almost obsessive amount of thought into every corner. And the staff? Wonderful. Friendly, genuinely warm, and exceptionally well-trained without ever feeling overly formal.

I’ve stayed at quite a few five-star hotels and boutique hotels, but this one really stood out to me. It happens to match my personal taste almost perfectly—which, of course, is the most dangerous kind of hotel!

I would especially recommend it to honeymooners and couples who want something intimate, romantic, stylish, and full of character rather than another huge, flashy hotel where you feel like one of several hundred guests.

I absolutely loved my stay here. If I come back to this area, I already know where I’ll be staying. No need to look around—I’ve found my hotel!

I had the great pleasure of using Mira's services today. She's the best in the world! 😊 Complete professionalism, charm, and a smile. I chose two completely different treatments, and both were performed perfectly.

Mira – warmest regards and thank you! I recommend you wholeheartedly.

And judging by the attention to detail evident in every aspect of the hotel's operation, I'm convinced that the other spa staff also represent an equally high standard.

A place is made of people, and that's no different here. We have the pleasure of living in a place where the staff are warm, welcoming, and helpful. They respond quickly, offer support, and sometimes I feel like they read my mind.

It's definitely a place you want to return to.

This is a wonderful place! We spent two days at the hotel and felt right at home.

Firstly, this is the best hotel on the island; we researched other options, and I can confirm it. The hotel is located on the edge of the beach, in a quiet and clean area. There's a coral reef in the water, and you can rent a mask and snorkel to swim to the neighboring beach.

Secondly, the level of service is simply incredible! First, the owner helped us book boat tickets, and then helped us change our dates when we decided to stay an extra night. The receptionist was a gem. She treated us to fruit, let us use the hotel grounds as if they were her own, and showered us with attention.

Thirdly, the rooms are simply wonderful. We stayed in two different rooms, and both were excellent, very clean, the beds were soft and comfortable. Each room has a panoramic view of the beach and sea. The only drawback I would highlight is the weak air conditioning in one of the rooms. I would recommend checking the coolant. Otherwise, I'm seriously thinking about coming for a longer period.

text:
Stayed one night at this homestay and were honestly very disappointed.

The rooms are essentially metal boxes—more like bunkers—with no windows, which makes them heat up a lot during the day. They’re also extremely poorly insulated; you can hear everything from neighboring rooms, even small movements like someone turning in bed.

The whole setup felt quite confusing and unorganized. We had to pay upfront, and some people handed us the key, but it wasn’t clear if they were actually responsible for the place. There was no proper welcome, no real communication, and no checkout process at all.

The property itself feels randomly put together: a tent in the back, constant watering in the front area, a huge table with no clear purpose, and some scattered plants. Overall, it lacks structure and feels a bit strange and unfinished.

On top of that, there was loud music playing throughout the night, which made it hard to rest.

While the room was reasonably clean, it definitely doesn’t justify the price—especially compared to other places in Vietnam. For what you get, it feels significantly overpriced.

Would not recommend staying here.

text:
Do not stay here. You will regret it.
Descriptions on Booking do not match what you get when you arrive. The management will apologise for adding the wrong descriptions for rooms and then blame you for taking their word for truth and not checking the photos. "Garden view" - no such thing. The room has no windows. "Futon" now means a cheap foam mattress thrown directly on the floor. "Terrace" is a shallow step to put your shoes on. This business is riding on the back of one single good room and stretching the truth until it snaps. They have a total mismatch with their clientele and their idyllic surroundings. This was an extremely jarring experience. A relaxing rural retreat this was not!

We thought this place would be chill and that we would be able to spend the cooler morning hours on the grounds enjoying the views... But instead, we were kept up until 2am by a group of rude, rowdy, drunk guests. The management should have made sure that this did not happen. They did not. In fact, they lied and told us the loud music and accompanying human noise (screeching loudly to be heard on top of the awful music blasting out of the provided speaker) would be dealt with before 10pm. It went on until almost midnight, after which the human screeching and beer drinking continued uninterrupted until after 2am.

Not only was our night ruined but so too was our next day. After finally getting to sleep in our corrugated metal box room with no windows, we awoke (much later than planned) to find the same guests colonising the shared space yet again - although this time hung over, a lot quieter and commandeering all of the cooling electric fans. It was too hot to try to enjoy anything as it approached midday. We left quickly.

This was a terrible, terrible, terrible experience.

Avoid at all costs!

text:
I chose to stay at the resort with my family at a rather rushed time, and I didn't have much time to research it beforehand like I usually do when planning a trip.

However, upon arrival, I was extremely satisfied. Initially, I thought the place would be just average, but that afternoon, while cycling around (bicycles are available for guests at the resort – there are many, and the borrowing/returning process is very reasonable based on resort regulations. For example, my two-room villa had four bikes parked in front of the villa), I realized how vast the grounds are. The villa I booked was only located at the very beginning, near the main entrance and lobby area...
The accommodation area is further inside (with electric carts to take guests in and out)... and there are many other accommodation options inside, including rooms on the hill and hotel-style rooms (which are more affordable and offer more choices)... and they all share the same amenities as the common swimming pool and other shared facilities.

The weather wasn't ideal when we went, with dark clouds covering the sky... but towards evening, the sky cleared up 😅 which helped salvage the beautiful scenery. We were able to admire the clouds, the sunset (it would be even better on a clear day) over Tam Giang Lagoon.

The room service was good. The only problem my family encountered was that the air conditioner in our room was leaking water, requiring a technician to fix it, which interrupted our plans a bit. However, everything was understandable because the staff were very friendly and attentive.

I noticed that there weren't many staff members, but they were always quick to assist guests when needed.

In the evening, you can eat at the resort or walk to the restaurants in front where there are local specialties with a pretty good seafood menu.

Breakfast at the hotel was abundant and luxurious. The breakfast buffet didn't have too many dishes, but it satisfied all tastes and offered choices for my family, from children to the elderly.

My family really enjoyed this place and would definitely choose to return again soon.

text:
My wife, daughter and I spent two wonderful nights at Pilgrimage Village Resort, and it was undoubtedly one of the highlights of our trip to Vietnam.

After the busy streets of Hanoi and Da Nang, and before heading to the lively chaos of Saigon, this place was exactly what we needed. A true oasis of peace and relaxation.

The resort is simply stunning. The lush gardens, beautiful flowers, swimming pools and every little corner of the outdoor areas create an incredible atmosphere of calm and beauty. Just walking around the property is a pleasure.

Our villa was exceptional. Spotlessly clean, beautifully decorated, spacious and extremely comfortable. Even the smallest details had been considered, including mosquito treatment in the room to ensure a peaceful night's sleep. And the bathroom? Absolutely enormous! Beautifully designed, incredibly well equipped and finished with exceptional taste and attention to detail.

Breakfast was another highlight. An amazing selection of fresh, high-quality food, with pretty much everything you could wish for.

The staff deserve special recognition. Everyone was incredibly friendly, attentive and professional, always available when needed but never intrusive. That perfect balance of hospitality that makes you feel truly welcome.

And I cannot finish this review without mentioning two experiences that made our stay even more special.

First, the massages! We received 30 minutes of complimentary massage for each night of our stay, meaning a full hour per person over our two nights. The lady who treated me was absolutely fantastic. Without exaggeration, one of the best massages I have ever had!

Second, the 7 AM beginner's Tai Chi session. What a wonderful way to start the day! Practising Tai Chi surrounded by such beautiful and peaceful surroundings was an experience I genuinely believe everyone should try at least once.

Pilgrimage Village is much more than just a hotel. It is a place where you can slow down, disconnect from the outside world and simply enjoy being there.

Would I return? Without the slightest hesitation. And next time, I would definitely stay longer!

Thank you to the entire team for making our family stay so memorable.

text:
Ancient Hue Garden Houses – A Hue experience even more beautiful than expected! 🌿

I was truly surprised by how much more beautiful and luxurious Ancient Hue was than I had anticipated! Before arriving, I thought it would just be a traditional garden-style hotel, but once inside, I realized how meticulously and exquisitely it's been designed.

Nestled in the Kim Long area, Ancient Hue embodies the beauty of old Hue houses, with its ancient tiled roofs, intricate wood carvings, courtyards, and lush green gardens. Traditional architecture is cleverly combined with modern amenities, creating a space that is both classic and luxurious without being ostentatious.

What I liked most was the sense of privacy and tranquility. Everything is gentle and elegant, from the decor and colors to the harmony between architecture and nature. The sophistication of Ancient Hue doesn't lie in its flashiness but in its profound aesthetic sense, making you feel like you're in an old Hue mansion rather than a typical hotel.

This time, I arrived in Hue during the rainy season. The sky was overcast, the trees were a deep green, and the rain-soaked tiled roofs added to the tranquil and romantic atmosphere. There was no need to go far; just sitting and admiring the garden, listening to the rain, was enough to make the trip worthwhile.

Ancient Hue is not only beautiful but also soulful. It's a place to stay that truly embodies Hue's unique character, luxurious in its own way, and far exceeded my expectations. 💚

If you consider the Kim Long restaurant upstairs separately, all the services are fine, the service is good, and the food is delicious, deserving of more customers. But the Van Xuan bar downstairs has a rather disappointing service attitude; they pay more attention to Western customers than Vietnamese customers. They take orders, confirm them, then leave, which is very unprofessional.

text:
Quite easily the best hotel I've ever stayed in. Service was impeccable, with friendly and warm staff diligently attending to our every need. The architecture, grounds and rooms are beautiful - especially the restaurant and the bar area.

We opted for a room with a private pool, and were pleasantly surprised that it was cleaned twice daily including mopping the floors, which was a nice touch. The pool was incredibly clean and a delight to use, secreted away under giant plants which made for a lovely ambience.

Given our love of Vietnamese food, we were surprised to find that the restaurant here provided some of the best, authentic meals we've eaten in the country. Breakfast was included, a la carte and unlimited, and the quality was miles above that of standard breakfast buffets elsewhere. We usually ordered three dishes between us to share, as well as iced coffees and infused teas or fresh juices, and staff would routinely ask if we wanted more.

Both breakfast and dinner had a wide selection available, and we felt this did not come at the cost of quality. We tried noodle soups, duck confit, chilli grouper, clams, shrimp in Thai sauce, fried rice, banh mi, bun bo hue... I even had a cheeseburger for breakfast out of curiosity, and it was so good I had to order a second one!

It also has to be said that the opening times of the restaurant are much appreciated - breakfast served until 10:00, and dinner until 22:00, allows for so much flexibility when it comes to going out on day tours, or wanting a lie-in.

Finally, the hotel were very helpful in organising a transfer to our next hotel in Hoi An. They had an itinerary planned, and the price was competitive with similar excursions on Booking.com. This gave us lovely peace of mind!

The only downside would be that the location of the hotel is not within easy walking distance of many of the attractions or eateries of Hue, but with ease of travel through apps like Grab this is a very minor issue.

We already wanted to come back to Vietnam after this holiday, and this accomodation has made that even more likely. I would recommend that anyone coming here stays at Ancient Hue Garden Houses!

Traveling to Hue during the Mid-Autumn Festival in 2026 was wonderful, thanks to the friendly and warm welcome from everyone at the hotel. Thank you to the hotel staff for giving me such a fun and memorable experience.

text:
I had a very memorable stay at Melody Riverside Homestay. The homestay was clean, quiet, and the rooms were tidy and well-equipped. The location was convenient, and the space near the river was very airy and relaxing.

What impressed me most was the hospitality of Mr. Phong and his children. The whole family was friendly, enthusiastic, and always ready to help guests with even the smallest things. Thanks to their thoughtfulness and warmth, I felt right at home.

If I have the chance to return to Hue, I will definitely choose Melody Riverside Homestay again. It's well worth experiencing, and I will recommend it to my friends and family. Thank you, Mr. Phong and your family, for providing such a wonderful stay!

The hostel is nice, affordable, and the breakfast is good. However, the location is quite far from the city centre, so for me it wasn't worth it. After reading the reviews, I expected more of a homestay atmosphere and a closer connection with the owner. He was kind, but I didn't feel he was very interested in interacting with the guests, so it didn't have the welcoming feeling I was expecting. Overall, the service is good, but I think the human side of the experience could be improved. Also, keep in mind that if you don't want to walk 30–40 minutes to reach the centre, you'll need to rent a scooter, as they don't provide bicycles anymore.

text:
The host, Mr. Phuong, and his family run this hostel out of his family home alongside his wife and daughter. It is located just off of the serene Hue city.

The venue is aptly placed within 15 minutes of most locations and easy to find. Mr. Phuong is tremendously easy to talk to and patient regarding touristy inquiries as he has 13 years of hostel host experience in Downtown Hue prior to running the location out of his residence.

While the room could be better ventilated and the bathroom amenities modernized, the beds are clean and the location can't be easily beat.

Today I attended the International Conference on HALAL Tourism Development: International Experiences and Current Situation in Hue City. During lunch, the organizers provided enough food for all tables, but for some reason, most tables received dessert while mine did not. The staff were nearby but didn't seem to notice. We waited a long time and eventually had to leave. I didn't need the dessert plate, but I was dissatisfied with the food preparation.

Your comments regarding the swimming pool have also been taken very seriously, as the safety and well-being of our guests are always our highest priority. Our pool has different depths ranging from 1.6 metres to 2.7 metres, with a lifeguard on duty daily from 6:00 to 21:00. We are pleased to know that you were safe following the incident. Nevertheless, we will reinforce our communication with the team to ensure that guests are clearly informed of the pool depths and lifeguard service hours, while maintaining close attention to pool safety at all times.
