I was especially unhappy with the receptionist who wore braces; she was very rude. As soon as I arrived, she told me I had to check out at 11:30 AM, even though the app I booked indicated a 12:00 AM check-out. I've always stayed at hotels with check-in times of 2 PM and check-out times of 12 AM. I said, "I see you don't have to check out until 12 AM," and she replied, "No, please check out at 11:30 AM." I didn't say anything more because my work was finished around 10 AM the next morning. But I started to think the service was terrible. Then I asked the staff if I could check out at 12 PM via the app because my child was sweating. text:
If you’re looking for an unforgettable Vietnamese dining experience, this hidden gem of a restaurant is a must-visit. Specializing in both shredded chicken and fried chicken dishes, the menu offers an incredible balance of flavors and textures that capture the essence of traditional Vietnamese cuisine.

First visit I ordered the shredded chicken, and it was nothing short of spectacular. The tender chicken was perfectly seasoned, I was shown how to mix the lime with salt and the dressing added a tangy and savory punch, making every bite refreshing and satisfying.

My next visit, I couldn’t resist the fried chicken.
Crispy on the outside and juicy on the inside, this dish is a perfect example of how simplicity done right can create something extraordinary. The chicken was served with a side of salad, orange rice along with a flavorful dipping sauce that perfectly complemented the crispy skin and succulent meat.

The portions were generous, prices are very affordable and the staff were incredibly welcoming, providing top-notch service. The restaurant itself has a cozy, relaxed atmosphere, making it the perfect spot for a casual meal with friends or family.

I have dined in and also ordered takeout on a few occasions, never been disappointed either way.

Highly recommended for anyone looking to enjoy authentic Vietnamese flavors in a warm, friendly setting!

trip_context: {"Order type": "Dine in", "Meal type": "Dinner"}
text:
While craving banh mi, I stumbled upon this shop along the way. Although the name seemed different from the Google listing, the location and opening hours matched Nha Viet.

We arrived for dinner around 6 pm, and the shop was still open.

Inside, there was ample seating, and al fresco seating was available along the road. However, numerous vendors approached us while dining in al fresco.

We ordered the two recommended banh mi options suggested by the counter staff, which did not disappoint.

The meat was pork and a mix of other meats, if I recall correctly. The meat was tender and flavorful, complemented by seasoned vegetables that enhanced its taste.

Everything was delicious, with crunchy bread on the outside and soft on the inside.

The serving time was fast, and the portion size was reasonable for the price. We also ordered three drinks, all of which were excellent. The options included an avocado shake, mango yogurt, and hot cocoa, none of which were overly sweet. However, the temperature of the hot cocoa was lukewarm, rather than hot, despite my request for it to be extra hot. I suppose this is typical in Vietnam.

Everything else was perfect.

**A must-try banh mi spot in Da Nang**
I had the chance to try the beef sausage (chả bò) and sunny-side-up egg banh mi at **Banh Mi - Bread Thao**, and it was truly a satisfying experience.

The baguette was freshly baked, crispy on the outside, and warm on the inside. The filling was generous and flavorful – the beef sausage was savory and well-seasoned, and the egg added a nice richness. Simple ingredients, but prepared with care and great balance.

The shop is clean and airy, and the service is friendly and welcoming. The staff speak English well, which makes it easy for international travelers to order. Prices are affordable and fair for both locals and tourists.

If you’re in Da Nang and looking for a high-quality, authentic banh mi, this place is definitely worth a visit.

An Absolutely Perfect Anniversary Dinner at Le Comptoir

Our 4th wedding anniversary dinner at Le Comptoir was truly a perfect experience.

From our email correspondence before the visit, to the warm welcome we received when we walked through the door, and all the way until we left, every moment was exceptional.

In particular, Myriam Moretto showed an extraordinary level of care and consideration toward my wife, who is 19 weeks pregnant.

Before we began the six-course menu, she thoughtfully considered the sauces, cooking methods, and harmony of the ingredients, and kindly modified several dishes for my wife, incorporating elements from the eight-course menu at no additional charge. It made us feel that we were receiving a truly special and personalized experience created just for us.

My wife was also able to enjoy a wine pairing experience alongside me, thanks to the team’s incredible kindness and patience. Even when I asked several times to confirm that the wine offered to her was truly 0.00% non-alcoholic, they responded with genuine warmth and professionalism.

We were equally impressed by the professionalism of the entire team. Every dish was explained with care and precision, and every course was served with remarkable attention to detail.

We would also like to express our sincere gratitude to the sommelier, who introduced each wine—from the sparkling and white wines to the reds—with such warmth, knowledge, and genuine pride in their work.

Although there were some language barriers, every member of the serving team continued to treat us with extraordinary kindness and consideration throughout the entire evening. Their hospitality truly touched us.

The evening ended beautifully with a special “Happy 4th Anniversary” lettering service, making our anniversary dinner absolutely perfect.

If we ever need a reason to come back to Da Nang, visiting Le Comptoir again will be one of the first reasons that comes to mind.

Thank you, from the bottom of our hearts, for the wonderful hospitality, thoughtfulness, and care you showed to both of us. You made our 4th wedding anniversary an unforgettable memory.

text:
Le Comptoir – An unforgettable signature tasting menu experience

We booked the Le Grand Menu Signature for a special dinner, and every single course was thoughtfully crafted, beautifully plated, and full of wonderful, layered flavours.

The meal started with delicate amuse-bouche, fresh BB Boudeuses oysters served on ice with a bright mignonette, paired with warm house-baked bread. Next came a stunning fish course in a clear aromatic broth, followed by the luxurious caviar dish, silky and balanced. The main pigeon was perfectly cooked, tender pink meat with rich fruit purée and nutty crunch that complemented the game beautifully.

The cheese selection was absolutely phenomenal — a huge curated table of French artisanal cheeses, from creamy bries to bold blues and aged hard cheeses, served with dried fruits, nuts and homemade preserves. The dessert sequence was such a lovely surprise: the wooden chocolate box engraved with Happy Wife Happy Life was such a charming touch, filled with handcrafted petit fours.

The open kitchen counter seating lets you watch the chefs work their magic, the service was attentive and knowledgeable, and the wine pairing worked seamlessly with every dish. This is fine dining with heart, not just pretty plates. Every bite felt intentional.

A wonderful night for a celebration. Highly recommend the signature grand menu if you love classic French gastronomy with refined modern touches. Will absolutely return!

text: We visited this restaurant yesterday. We booked a table in advance via Instagram, and there were no issues with that; they responded quickly. We specifically chose the fourth-floor terrace so we could watch the Dragon Bridge show in the evening. The waitstaff were friendly and tried to resolve issues promptly. That pretty much sums up the positives of the place. My child ordered the Marsala Gnocchi but couldn't finish it; I couldn't finish it either after trying his portion—it was incredibly salty. Then again, I’m just sharing our experience; perhaps some people actually like it that way. We spent a long time choosing a pizza and eventually ordered the Meat Lover Pizza. That was a huge mistake. The pizza was incredibly spicy. I generally dislike spicy food—even just a little bit. There was no indication on the menu that this pizza was spicy, even though other items did have such notes. I urge you to add a spicy label to the menu for this pizza so other guests don't end up as disappointed as I was yesterday (assuming they don't like spicy food, of course). It was a very unpleasant surprise. They offered to replace the pizza with a non-spicy one for free, but the experience was already ruined. They also offered a complimentary cocktail, but we declined; we didn't want anything else at that point. The only good thing about the pizza was the dough—it was actually excellent. Overall, the food was terrible. I would never come back here. I really regret choosing this place.

From the moment we walked in we knew we were going to have a good night. Straight away the owner came over and introduced himself. It was amazing to hear and see how passionate he is about his restaurant and his customers. This restaurant is located with an amazing view of the dragon bridge. Our food did take an hour to come out, however, it was worth it!! The lasagne is amazing! The owner compensated due to the wait time and let us up on the terrace to watch the dragon bridge show! I would recommend booking in advance to get a table on the terrace if you are wanting to see the show as there is limited seating and the restaurant is very busy! I have to give credit to the staff too who were so attentive and helpful.

text:
Undoubtedly, this is an experience worth trying. And I can say for sure — it’s not for everyone. For people who love Michelin restaurants, it’s often more about the label, where the food frequently does not match the quality that is claimed. Yes, Michelin today is largely a commercial story.

Now, about this place we visited today — this is a story about real quality, about details, which is the most important thing. Yes, details. And for those who are actually able to appreciate them. These details include the service — and I would even say synchronized service — the quality of the food itself, the presentation, and of course the interior and the intimacy. Because intimacy is key here.

There are only three tables on the second floor. We’ve already been here once with friends from our group. And downstairs there are two tables: one for two people and one for a small group. So in total, the restaurant serves only three tables. Just imagine that. The entire kitchen and the entire staff work exclusively for you. Can you imagine that? Yes, you can — in places like this.

This is not for people who love flashy social gold. This is for those who truly know how to appreciate what is offered here. This is my second time at this restaurant, and I’m sure I’ll come back again and again, because now I live in Da Nang. And this is one of my absolute favorite places. Yes, it may not be a place for everyday dining due to the cost, but why not allow yourself such exceptional cuisine from time to time?

From what we ate, my absolute favorite was the lamb. The lamb here is prepared in the best way I have ever tried in my life. And it turns out — I do like lamb after all. In other places, I didn’t. I can say with certainty: this is the best lamb I’ve ever eaten.

As for the steak: it was most likely cooked sous-vide. And it’s simply fantastic. Excellent meat, excellent quality. There is absolutely no sense of freezing and defrosting. Everything is served exactly as it should be. And I’m saying this as someone who lives in Argentina — the country of meat. This is one of the best steaks I’ve ever had in my life. Even better than the ones I cook myself.

Of course, the tartare. The tartare is done beautifully. Everything is correct, with an excellent recipe. This is something that only people who truly love tartare can appreciate. We also tried the seasonal fish. The portion was small, but everything was very flavorful and well executed. And the risotto — truffle risotto — simply brilliant. Brilliantly made, delivering pleasure to every single taste receptor.

In fact, I’ve tried almost everything at this restaurant. We also tried the set menu before. I liked about 70–80% of the dishes in the set menu. Around 20% were just okay. But overall, the set menu is still a very good alternative for those who want to try everything at once. Not everything from the main menu, of course — it’s a separate selection — but it’s a very solid experience that deserves attention.

Now about alcohol. This is definitely the weak point. Some of the alcohol here is spoiled. Some of it, frankly speaking, does not match the level of the food at all. That’s why the second time, we didn’t drink alcohol. And honestly, everything is great even without it.

I understand that Vietnam is not Argentina or France, so wine culture is simpler here. And another reason the wine is spoiled is likely not the restaurant itself, but the supply chain — from producer countries to distributors and then to restaurants. I’ve noticed this not for the first time in Asia: much of the alcohol, especially red wine, is spoiled or sour. Red wine cannot be kept for more than a few hours at temperatures above 22–24°C. That’s something to keep in mind.

Overall, this is an experience that truly deserves attention. And I recommend it to those who are genuinely capable of appreciating it.

We decided to share everything, which turned out to be the way to go. The steak was perfectly prepared, with a quality cut and excellent cook. The General Tso’s chicken special was packed with flavor, but the Wagyu Reuben sandwich was sublime. Easily one of those dishes where you take the first bite, look across the table, and immediately know you’re both thinking the same thing. The kitchen team clearly knows what they’re doing—not only with flavor and technique, but with beautiful presentation as well.

We paired everything with two fresh juices and somehow found room to finish with a gorgeous lemon tart, which was the perfect bright ending to a seriously satisfying meal.

The staff were incredible throughout our visit—friendly, attentive, and genuinely welcoming. Between the professional kitchen team, quality ingredients, presentation, and service, The Nomad Kitchen punches well above a casual neighborhood restaurant.

If you’re staying around An Thuong in Da Nang, put this one on your list. Come hungry, order a few things to share, and do not skip that Wagyu Reuben.

Highly recommended. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

The menu is Mediterranean-inspired, and honestly, the food was 10/10. There wasn’t a meal we didn’t love!
We HIGHLY recommend both the pan seared scallops and lamb skewer from the mains - both were cooked to perfection.
As Australians, we are spoilt for choice back home. But this meal has surpassed even some of the better restaurants back home.
On top of a great meal, the service was phenomenal, and the views were epic!
We cannot wait to return to Da Nang to come back to The Gypsy!

text:
My wife and I had dinner at Gypsy for my wife's birthday on Friday April 24th, 2026. From the moment we walked through the entryway we knew the night would be something special. The service was exceptional - staff constantly ready to top up glasses etc, without being in any way intrusive. The food was beautifully prepared, cooked and presented and was absolutley delicious. Chef prepared a special amuse bouche which was divine. We started with oysters and the goat's cheese salad. Although the oysters are a little smaller than we are used to in Australia, they were excellent. The goat's cheese salad was delicious. For mains, I had the mushroom rigatoni and my wife had the seafood risotto and they were both absolutely delicious. The wine list was pretty extensive and reasonably priced for Vietnam, where wines can be quite expensive. We finished off with the blueberry cheesecake, presented with the staff all singing "Happy Birthday".
We had such a great night that as we were walking out, we made another booking for our last night in Danang. We highly recommend Gypsy rooftop - it was a sensational experience.
Update; we returned on Monday night 4th May 2026. The scallop tartare was delicious, as was the salmon spaghetti. Service was again sensational. We will definitely be back next time we visit Danang.

I decided to come to Gypsy Rooftop because I thought it was cool spot to see the city of Đa Nang from. I have to say that this spot blew my socks off. The poolside lounge has a 180° view of the city and is tastefully decorated with an option to dine inside the restaurant.

The restaurant offers a fusion of Mediterranean cuisine with a Vietnamese flare. I ordered the waygu linguine and my partner ordered the truffle rigatoni. The noodles we done to perfection, the meat portion was plenty, and the PORTIONS were rather large (I can't believe I'm writing this :o). The servers ended up adding more truffle aioli to my partners dish, which we thought was a hit overkill, as the rigatoni was quite rich.

I honestly think that the portions could be a little bit smaller because the dishes are rich with flavours that it is impossible to eat the whole thing; the prices should also reflect the smaller portion sizes.

The service was top notch. All the servers spoke english and we're well versed in suggesting wine pairings to along with the dishes. My partner absolutely loved the cocktails he had there. Needless to say, we'll be going back before we leave.

text:
Ponte Cafe & Eatery was such a beautiful brunch experience in Da Nang. The atmosphere immediately caught our attention — peaceful, clean, cozy, and relaxing with the greenery and koi pond right by the window. It was the perfect little spot to sit, eat, and enjoy the scenery.

We ordered the salmon with a fresh side salad, sourdough bread, and scrambled eggs on the side. Everything came out fresh, beautifully presented, and delicious. The salmon was especially good, and the scrambled eggs were cooked just right. Our drinks were also refreshing and paired perfectly with the meal.

Now let me tell you about the owner/waitress — she was funny, welcoming, and sweet to the bone! Her personality made the experience even better. After we finished eating, she even gave us food so we could feed the koi fish outside. That little touch turned brunch into a whole experience and made the visit feel extra special.

The food was great, the service was warm, and the atmosphere was beautiful. This is absolutely a place I would return to while in Da Nang. 5 stars all the way.

We had the bacon and egg muffin and a banana strawberry smoothie, both were really really good! Simple but so yummy. The staff were so friendly too. Would definitely come back!

Update : we came back again and tried more drinks this time. The blueberry crush, white coffee and mango yogurt. They were all really good too, but the blueberry crush was definitely my fav 🤤 so so good! Still one of our favorite spots and service is always lovely :)

text:
Extremely disappointing experience absolutely not worth the hype.
Visited after seeing the great Google reviews and drove around 5 km specifically to have dinner here. Unfortunately, the experience was pathetic from the food to the staff’s attitude.

I ordered a basic paneer dish and rotis, and both were extremely disappointing. The paneer tasted like frozen tomato gravy that had simply been reheated with paneer thrown into it. No proper masala, no flavour, no effort. It tasted like something from a very average local dhaba, not a restaurant with such high ratings.The rotis were equally bad paper-thin, poorly cooked and completely below average.
To make matters worse, the staff member taking the order had a very poor attitude when I gave honest feedback. Instead of listening, he seemed unnecessarily offended.What is the point of customer feedback if you are not willing to accept it?

I honestly don't understand how this place has such high ratings. For me, it was a complete waste of time, money and energy, and it completely spoiled the evening. Would definitely not recommend it.
owner_reply:
Dear Madam,

Thank you for sharing your feedback. We are sorry to hear that your experience did not meet your expectations.

First, regarding the Paneer dish, we would like to clarify that all our gravies are prepared FRESH every day in our kitchen. We do not use frozen gravy and simply reheat it with paneer added. We take pride in serving freshly prepared food to our customers.

Regarding the roti, our rotis are intentionally thin, which is our usual style (and our naan is prepared in the same style). We do not use yeast or baking powder to make them thick like some other restaurants. This is how we have always prepared our bread, and most of our customers are very happy with it.

During your visit, when you shared your feedback, our staff politely tried to make both of you happy by offering to replace the roti and Lachha Paratha that you had ordered. We also have CCTV cameras in the restaurant, so the interaction can be reviewed. From our side, we genuinely tried to assist you and did not intend to show any attitude or disrespect.

We serve many customers every day, including large groups, and we regularly receive positive feedback about our food and service. Of course, we understand that everyone's taste and expectations are different, and perhaps we simply could not match your expectations on this occasion.

We respect your opinion, but we also feel it is unfair to judge the entire restaurant based mainly on ONE CURRY and the BREAD. Nevertheless, we appreciate your feedback and will continue doing our best to provide fresh food and friendly service to all our customers.

We are sorry that our food and style were not suitable for your taste, and we hope you have a better dining experience elsewhere.

Regards,
Manvar Rasoi Team

text:
🐶☕Little Dogs Coffee and Cake Cafe

I wish I could give it higher than 5 stars.

Since we started slow traveling, one thing we really miss is having a dog. So we made a special trip to Little Dogs Coffee and Cake Cafe, and let me tell you, it was one of the best decisions we have made in Da Nang!

When we first arrived, we were a little disappointed because there were no dogs around. The owner must have noticed because she went and got the dogs for us! 🥹 That absolutely made our day. They were so friendly and excited to be petted, and we could have spent hours with them. The owner was just as wonderful, taking the time to talk with us and making us feel so welcome.

Honestly, at that point, I didn't even care if the coffee and pastries were any good. We were already having such a great experience!

BUT LET ME TELL YOU... the food and drinks did not disappoint! The salted coffee was easily one of the best we have had so far in Da Nang. We also tried a Vietnamese iced coffee, and we shared a pound cake filled with whipped cream, fresh strawberries, and strawberry puree. The cake was simply perfect, with just the right amount of sweetness to go along with our coffees. ☕🍰

And did I mention the prices? Ridiculously good!

We usually enjoy trying a different coffee shop every morning, but this place is going to be an exception. We are already talking about making regular trips back, getting our dog fix, and trying some of their banh mi sandwiches next time.

This is exactly what I love about Vietnam. It's not just about the food or the places you visit. It's the people, the little unexpected experiences, and the places that make you feel at home even when you're halfway around the world.

I honestly wish we had a cozy, inviting place like this back in Las Vegas. Until then, we'll just have to keep coming back here! 🐶❤️

If you're in Da Nang and love dogs, good coffee, delicious cake, and genuinely friendly people, put this place on your list. You won't regret it!

place: Trần Khuê Restaurant - Cù Lao Chàm
text:
Very Disappointing Experience

We booked a snorkeling trip the day before and were told to come at 10 AM. They said a fisherman would take just the two of us to the reef for 45 minutes, then bring us back — sounded great. But when we arrived, no one spoke English, and it took ages to even understand what we were there for. We were told to come back at 10:45, and suddenly it turned into a full group tour with guides and lots of people. Totally not what we were promised.

We ended up on a speedboat that stopped at two other places first to drop off people, then finally took us to the reef. The spot itself was beautiful — but people were literally stepping on the corals, and when we told the guides, they either ignored us or said they didn’t care. We were allowed to snorkel for just 20 minutes, then had to sit on the boat again while they picked up the rest of the group.

To make it worse, we were overcharged — the sign said 100,000 VND per person, but we paid 300,000 VND for the two of us because we thought we were getting a private trip. It was absolutely not what we were told. After the trip, we asked for the 100,000 VND difference back, and luckily they gave it to us — but overall, it was a frustrating and disappointing experience. Wouldn’t recommend at all.

text:
We dropped by for lunch and had the whole place to ourselves because they seem to focus mostly on the dinner crowd. Keep in mind there is no A/C, so it gets incredibly hot during the day. I would highly recommend coming for dinner instead.
The crab soup with greens (Ghẹ nấu rau muống) was excellent. The greens actually tasted more like sweet potato leaves than morning glory. The crab meat was remarkably sweet and fresh, and the broth had a subtle spicy kick that really opened up our appetite.
The seafood fried glass noodles (Miến xào hải sản) featured incredibly sweet pineapple chunks, and the noodles absorbed all the savory flavors beautifully. It came loaded with shrimp, squid, and wood ear mushrooms, making for a perfectly balanced savory dish.
For the salt and pepper mantis shrimp (Tôm tít rang muối), the owner went above and beyond by helping us peel them, which was amazing service. The shrimp were packed with rich roe.
We also tried the lemongrass stir-fried clams (Hến xào). The herbal flavor was a bit too intense for my personal liking, but it came with a complimentary baguette for dipping into the sauce. The bread had a lovely buttery aroma and tasted delicious.
To top it all off, they even treated us to a complimentary plate of watermelon at the end of our meal. Great food and fantastic service.

text:
Among the seafood joints in Da Nang, Be Nu holds a curious place.
It sits in Alley 267 Ngo Quyen. The place is small. It has the feel of the outskirts of Hoi An, or some familiar village back in Quang Nam. A quiet patch of sky hangs over the tables. Low brick walls run around the yard. In the corner, a jackfruit tree bends under the weight of its fruit. Further off, in the neighbor’s yard, a mango tree stands heavy with green fruit, drawing every eye.
The seafood tanks are bright and clean.
By six in the evening, the tables begin to fill. Chinese, Vietnamese, Westerners. They come because of the good words written about the place on the internet.
I ordered the pufferfish stewed with turmeric, mantis shrimp in garlic butter, squid egg hotpot, grilled stingray, steamed clams, and tamarind crab. The food came fast. One dish after another, neat upon the table.
When the bill came, it was just a little over one million dong. Then, you understood why they keep coming back.

My family didn't go snorkeling, so we went to the restaurant to rest beforehand and asked for food early because we had children. The restaurant was okay. Suddenly, while we were eating, a staff member (a thin woman with a gaunt face) came out and said this wasn't our table and asked us to move to another table. We agreed, but she spoke very rudely, saying we sat there without asking anyone. I explained that we had already told them we were tour guide Phuc's group, but we didn't see anyone guiding us, and now they were blaming us. Anyway, I just wanted to keep the peace and only asked for food for the children to eat. But no, the restaurant staff made us wait for over an hour, until 1 PM, while other groups who arrived later got to eat first. After our tour guide returned, they complained that we were seated in the wrong place and had an unpleasant attitude (this was relayed by the tour guide).
It's unacceptable for service staff to have such a petty and resentful attitude towards customers. I wonder if the manager or owner of the restaurant is aware of this? But if the owner reads this review, please retrain your staff. In this day and age, you can tell immediately whether a service is good or not. text:
One of the best restaurants in town. We've been to more than 10, and this one is the best for Vietnamese food. The portions are good, and you're getting a nice amount of meat in them, which is something I learned to appreciate in Hoi An as a westerner used to consuming a fair amount of protein every day. Everything is seasoned but not overly so. The food is delicious, in our opinion.

This is a family-owned establishment, which is always great to support. The dogs are very cute. There are some nice little touches you can see that you won't find in other restaurants, for example, their plates, glasses, etc.

I did have some issues here, though. First was having a hair in one dish. And the second was not getting correct change once while the place was busy and kids were involved in handling it, but it was partly my fault that I didn't check it right away. But it was only 20k which I would've tipped anyway, so it wasn't a big deal.

All in all, you should definitely check this place out if you're in the area and want some tasty food. Just bear in mind that nobody is perfect and things happen.

Một trải nghiệm tồi tệ ; khách nước ngoài vào sau nhưng lên đồ trước khi cùng gọi bugger; đoàn nhà mình vào ăn xong vẫn chưa lên nổi đồ nhưng vẫn đòi thanh toán tiền nói bảo giảm 10% nhưng mình đâu cần ; thái độ phục vụ tệ . A truly disappointing experience.

Our group arrived first and ordered at the same time as another group of foreign customers who came in later. However, their food was served before ours, while we had to wait a long time without receiving our meals.

What disappointed us even more was that the staff asked us to pay the bill before all of our food had even been served. They offered a 10% discount, but that wasn’t the point. We were looking for professional service and basic respect for customers—not a discount to make up for poor service.

The service was unprofessional, disorganized, and the staff’s attitude was disappointing. I hope the management takes this feedback seriously and improves both the service quality and staff training to prevent other customers from having the same experience.

Fourth, recognizing this as a restaurant error, we have PROACTIVELY REDUCED the total bill by 10% as an apology and to compensate for the inconvenience you experienced. This is a voluntary offer from the restaurant and is NOT intended to AVOID RESPONSIBILITY for the mistake that occurred.

Finally, we would like to affirm that Minh's Kitchen DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE BETWEEN VIETNAMESE AND FOREIGN CUSTOMERS. From the moment you arrived, our staff welcomed you, seated you, and served you with the same enthusiasm as all other guests. The order of service depends on the kitchen's food preparation process and unforeseen incidents such as this instance of bringing the wrong dish, and is not based on the customer's nationality.

We always value all feedback and see it as an opportunity to improve the quality of our services. Once again, we sincerely apologize for the mistake that occurred and thank you for taking the time to provide feedback. Thank you for listening.

place: Monkey Homestay & Bar - Local Seafood & Cocktails
trip_context: {"Trip type": "Vacation"}
text:
The three days I spent at Monkey Homestay were the highlight of my entire trip to Da Nang.

Cham Island is peaceful and unspoiled, making it the perfect place to slow down, relax, and simply enjoy island life. One of the best parts of staying here was the food. Monkey Homestay has, in my opinion, the best chef on the island, using incredibly fresh ingredients. I ordered the crab every day because it was so delicious, the fried rice was amazing, and the fresh orange juice was rich, refreshing, and perfect for the hot weather.

The room was simple but very clean. I especially loved the wooden flooring in the bathroom, and the shower area was spacious and comfortable.

If you’d like to explore the island, you can rent a scooter directly from the homestay. They even fill up the fuel tank for you, which makes everything so convenient.

Breakfast is served downstairs every morning, and it’s one of the best breakfasts you can find on the island. Since the weather gets hot very early in the summer, it’s great not having to go somewhere else just to eat. Waking up and enjoying a delicious breakfast right at the homestay was one of the best decisions we made.

I would definitely stay here again the next time I visit Cham Island.

We visited Mr Dung on a Monday night and were pleasantly surprised by how relaxed and welcoming the atmosphere was. The restaurant was not very busy, which made for a comfortable and unhurried dinner. From the moment we walked in, the family-owned vibe was obvious. The staff were friendly, attentive, and genuinely warm in the way they greeted us.
We were told upfront that only smaller-sized lobsters were available that day. We decided to go ahead and order the local lobster, cooked in garlic butter, and it absolutely did not disappoint. The portions were good value, the meat was succulent and generous, and the garlic butter added just the right amount of richness without overwhelming the natural sweetness of the lobster.

Alongside the lobster, we ordered the morning glory and the white rose. Both were delicious and well-executed. The morning glory had a nice crunch and light seasoning, while the white rose dumplings were delicate, flavorful, and clearly made with care.

Overall, we are really happy we found Mr Dung. It is the kind of place that feels authentic, unpretentious, and focused on good food rather than hype. We will definitely be going back and recommending it to friends looking for a reliable, tasty seafood spot with a friendly, family-run feel.

We came because of the highly rated review and the fact you can actually pick out the seafood you’d want, making it feel fresher. Unfortunately in a region filled with delicious food, and a country known for flavors, this was probably our worst meal in our week long trip along the coast.

We ordered some mantis shrimp, fried squid, some mixed vegetables, and sea grab. The mantis shrimp was the better dish since having it fried at least helped to add some flavors. Everything else was bland and flavorless. The mixed vegetables seemed to have been simply boiled and dumped onto our plates. We had the sea crab which is arguably the smallest crab we have ever seen at a seafood restaurant — no wait staff helped us pick out the crab nor gave us heads up about the type of crab we will be getting. Upon service, we spoke to a wait staff and had it exchanged for a proper crab — it was larger but still came out flavorless.

Environment wise, there is the downstairs and we later learned, an upstairs. It appears that folks who’ve been here before have asked to be taken upstairs upon arrival. Perhaps the food is better up there? Maybe it’s an off day for the chef, but this being our last dinner of the trip, it was quite the downer & made us doubt Google reviews in the area going forward.
owner_reply:

text:
As others have noted, a great dinner, location and fish.

One of the best grilled fish (grouper) that I've had in Vietnam over the last 9 years. Prices are OK (it's Hoi An afterall). Our dinner cost a little over 9M VDN about US $35.

A few notes for those new to Vietnam. While my Vietnamese wife will buy fish at the market or near the sea at the crack of dawn for home cooking; eating out, a live fish is always selected that you can see and select.
Also, after we pick the fish (in this case about 2.3 kg), we ask that the fillet be grilled and the head and tail be put in "hot pot", (though my wife informs me that in this area of Vietnam it's not called hot pot because it comes with rice not noodles).
in any case, it like fish soup and this was one of the best ever fish soups I've had.
We also liked the friendly, helpful owner.

If in the Hoi An area and you want a wonderful dinner, lunch by the beach (they so have tables on the beach also for their customers) , go here, you get great value for your money and I promise you will not be disappointed.

text: Best com ga I've had in Hoi An! Truly a hidden gem and deserves more recognition. Rice and chicken portion is perfect. What makes them stand out from the other com ga is the added shredded green papaya and a secret sauce poured over the dish.

Chú Trung’s Chicken Rice is a hidden gem you definitely need to try when you’re in town! The food is delicious, with that authentic, homey flavor that you can only find at local spots. It’s super affordable too — we had two plates of chicken rice plus an extra portion of chicken, and the total was just around 100,000 VND!

The setup is simple and casual, with seating right on the sidewalk, giving it a very local and laid-back vibe. Just a heads-up: you should bring cash because Chú Trung doesn’t accept bank transfers. If you want real local flavors at a great price, don’t miss Chú Trung’s!

The vegetarian mains—the velvety pumpkin soup and the handmade mushroom ravioli—were outstanding and executed beautifully.
​With its great atmosphere and highly accommodating, attentive team, this restaurant is definitely a must-visit when you are in Hoi An.

text:
I went to this restaurant because of the raving reviews and because it’s close to where I’m staying, being in need of a good steak every now and then. Unfortunately it wasn’t what I hoped for. I ordered a flat iron steak, medium, but got it medium rare. I didn’t send it back to the kitchen, because that would only make it worse, because it was also already cut with the grain, which made it very chewy and stringy.
I did tell the staff about it when I they saw my plate, because I left all the raw pieces on it, but it made no difference. A gesture of trying to make it better, by that I mean maybe offering a drink or anything of that kind, would’ve been nice. Work in hospitality myself, so I know how these things can be.
My honest feedback: the difference between medium rare and medium is a very important one, and if the steak leaves the kitchen already cut, it should be cut correctly, against the grain; the slicing perpendicular to the muscle fibers. This shortens the fibers, making each bite more tender and easier to chew.
Loved the veggies though ;)

UPDATED:
The owner invited me to give his restaurant another chance, and I did.
I must say: the steak was perfectly medium, the veggies just as good as before and the service and atmosphere good.
Thank you Ti for your reaction and your invitation and the time you took to change my experience.
Will definitely come back while in Hoi An.
owner_reply:
Dear Hoed
I truly appreciate you taking the time to write such helpful feedback. It was a very negative experience for you at the restaurant (from unsatisfactory food to poor service). I will discuss this with our chef to minimize the chances of this happening again (frankly, they did a great job before, selling many steaks and receiving very positive reviews and satisfaction. I think your steak was the second time in three months that we haven't done as well as it should have, so the chef didn't perform well this time). The owner: Ti

text:
La Table Hoi An is, without a doubt, the best restaurant in Hoi An. The quality of the food was exceptional, and the entire experience felt very refined and thoughtfully curated.

We opted for the set menu with wine pairing, and the team were incredibly accommodating. As we don’t drink Prosecco, they immediately offered a French white wine alternative without any hesitation, which we really appreciated.

The dishes were outstanding — the foie gras was absolutely delicious, and my husband’s blue crab dish was equally impressive. We both had the steak for the main, which was cooked perfectly.

A small but notable detail — this was probably the only restaurant we visited in Vietnam (outside of Four Seasons or other five-star resorts) where we were thoughtfully asked whether we preferred still or sparkling water, which really reflects the level of service.

They also added a very sweet touch to acknowledge that we were on our honeymoon, making the evening even more special.

Highly recommend — an exceptional dining experience from start to finish.

Curious about french cuisine here in Hoi an.

Service and atmosphere is good. The starter has frozen cucumber juice with it which is interesting, but the flavour does not blend well with the jelly/ salad.

The main course fish has a unfresh texture, I would describe as mushy? I think it’s not about the cooking but the fish quality itself.

Pho dessert is very interesting, pho taste was recreated. I appreciate the creativity, but I don’t think it is delicious…

To summarise, I like the staff and the concept of this restaurant. But the food is a bit disappointing esp given the price.

Our best regards,
Team La Table

text: La Table Hoi An was a perfect experience. My wife and I came to visit Hoi An for the first time as a celebration for our 6th anniversary. As the only French meal we booked for the long weekend it absolutely did not disappoint. We were greeted warmly by Chef Pierre and his team, the food was delicious, the wine delightful, the decor cozy and comfortable. Would absolutely recommend La Table to everyone and we can’t wait to be back with our family in the future.

​I recently had one of the finest French dining experiences at La Table Hoi An, and it exceeded every expectation. From the moment you step in, the ambience sets a warm, sophisticated tone. Every element—the exquisite food, impeccable service, and a carefully curated wine and beverage list—was absolutely world-class.
​A special highlight of the evening was meeting Chef Pierre Emmanuel, who personally takes the time to step out of the kitchen and connect with guests during the meal. That personal touch elevates the experience from a simple dinner to something truly memorable.
​An unforgettable culinary gem. I cannot wait to return!

I had an amazing experience at this French restaurant in Vietnam. The food was absolutely delicious-every dish was thoughtfully prepared, and you can really tell the chef is highly skilled. The flavors were refined, well-balanced, and beautifully presented.
The service was just as impressive. The staff were attentive, friendly, and made the whole dining experience feel warm and welcoming.
What surprised me the most was the value for money. For this level of quality, the pricing is incredibly reasonable.
I would definitely recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a great French dining experience.

La Table is a great blend of French cuisine with local Vietnamese flavours and ingredients. The food was absolutely delicious - we had the spring menu: the homage to tomatoes starter, the duck (might I add, perfectly cooked), and for dessert the sweet Pho. I loved every single dish, the service was impeccable, and overall had a great time. On top of that, they accommodated my dairy allergy (which can be a challenge in French cuisine) and still managed to make some super tasty and beautiful dishes. Highly recommend :)

We dined at La Table Hoi An French Restaurant with high expectations, given its reputation as one of the top restaurants in Hoi An.

On the positive side, the service was good and attentive. The meat dish with foie gras was enjoyable, and the complimentary wine from the chef was a nice touch that added to the experience.

However, there were some disappointing elements. The crab starter with apple lacked flavor—the apple was served frozen, with little aroma or taste, and the dish overall was missing acidity and balance.

Overall, while there are some strong points, the experience did not fully meet expectations for a restaurant of this level.

Absolutely blew me away. I’ve had good coffee all over the world, but these guys are operating on another level.

I ordered the egg coffee first and… wow. It’s rich, silky, almost dessert-like without being heavy. Perfect balance of sweetness and that deep Vietnamese coffee punch. Easily the best egg coffee I’ve had in Vietnam.

Their pour-over was just as impressive clean, aromatic, and full of character. You can tell they’re roasting quality beans and actually care about the craft.

But the real standout was the service from Thanh Hà. Genuine warmth, great recommendations, and the kind of hospitality that makes you feel like you’ve been coming here for years.

If you’re in Hoi An and love coffee, this place is non-negotiable. Go for the egg coffee, stay for the pour-over, and enjoy some of the best service in town.

The pizza is the best, making it hard to order anything else. It’s cooked in a wood fire oven with freshly made dough and fresh local ingredients. Prices are in line with other restaurants nearby, but the quality is far better. We always dine in, and the staff are warm, attentive, and genuinely appreciative, which keeps us coming back.

The owners are a local Vietnamese family who live here like forever. They speak English well and can answer any questions you have.

text:
The Vietnamese food at this restaurant was one of the highlights of my trip and easily exceeded all of my expectations. From the moment the dishes arrived at the table, everything looked incredibly fresh, colorful, and carefully prepared. The vibrant herbs, perfectly cooked chicken, fragrant yellow rice, and crisp vegetables created a meal that was both visually appealing and packed with flavor. Every ingredient tasted fresh, and it was clear that great care had gone into preparing each dish. The balance of flavors was outstanding, with the freshness of the herbs complementing the savory chicken and the aromatic rice perfectly. Every bite offered something new, making the meal exciting from start to finish.

One of the things I appreciated most was how authentic everything tasted. Instead of overwhelming the food with heavy sauces or spices, the natural flavors of the ingredients were allowed to shine. The herbs added a refreshing taste, while the chicken was tender, juicy, and seasoned just right. The rice was fluffy, fragrant, and had a subtle richness that paired wonderfully with the rest of the meal. It was the kind of food that felt both comforting and satisfying without being overly heavy.

The service also made the experience even better. The staff were friendly, welcoming, and attentive throughout the meal. They made sure everything arrived quickly, answered any questions with a smile, and created a relaxed atmosphere that made dining enjoyable. Even though the restaurant was busy, the food came out promptly, showing how well organized the kitchen and staff were.

Another thing that stood out was the incredible value for money. Everything was reasonably priced, making it easy to enjoy a delicious, high-quality meal without spending a fortune. The generous portion sizes meant there was plenty of food, and considering the freshness of the ingredients and the overall quality, the prices felt more than fair. It’s rare to find a restaurant that combines authentic flavors, generous servings, and affordable prices so successfully.

The atmosphere of the restaurant added to the overall experience as well. It felt warm, clean, and inviting, making it a comfortable place to relax and enjoy a meal. Whether visiting with family or friends, it creates the perfect environment for sharing traditional Vietnamese dishes and experiencing the local culture through food.

Overall, this restaurant delivered an exceptional dining experience from beginning to end. The fresh ingredients, authentic flavors, excellent service, generous portions, welcoming atmosphere, and affordable prices all combined to create a memorable meal. It is the kind of place that leaves a lasting impression and makes you want to return again before your trip is over. I would highly recommend this restaurant to anyone visiting Vietnam who wants to experience delicious local cuisine at an excellent price. It perfectly showcases why Vietnamese food is loved around the world, and it was undoubtedly one of the best meals I have had during my visit.

text:
I came here five years ago, and it was some of the best Indian food I can remember. This time, though, the experience was more mixed. Some dishes were outstanding, while others were fairly plain.

We had the Northern vegetarian thali, a rava dosa, vermicelli dal, chicken biryani, naan, and lassi. The star of the show was definitely the rava dosa. It was light and flaky, with wonderful flavor, and the accompanying chutneys were excellent—especially the coconut chutney.

The thali had some good curries, but the rice was pretty boring, which made the overall dish disappointing. The vermicelli dal sounded particularly exciting and unique on the menu, but when it arrived, it was a stodgy, bland lump. I’d definitely avoid that one. The biryani was solid but nothing special, and the naan could have been puffier and flakier.

I’d definitely come back for more rava dosa, but I’d probably skip most of the other dishes.

text: It was soooo good I had to come back! I had their egg + avo toast both times and also tried their pain au chocolate! It was spot on, very fresh and filling as a brunch meal. text:
We’ve been in Hoi An for a few weeks, and this is by far the nicest place to have breakfast/lunch and work. The staff is super friendly, and the coffee is great. But what really makes it special is the free water, perfect for staying hydrated when you're working all day!

They also serve delicious sourdough, and yes, there is air conditioning and there is good wifi. There wasn't even any music playing, making it completely quiet and peaceful. I honestly don't have a single idea on how to improve this place for digital nomads.

We’ve spent many hours here.
Thank you 💛🫰

The atmosphere here is just like an upscale laid back beachside cafe should be, the AC is perfect, and we left wanting more.
Cheers Thom’s!

text: Lovely service and a delicious cinnamon roll was a good beginning, but the upstairs is a tremendous workspace! Lots of privacy plus free water and such a nice location with the ocean right out the window.

A magical Frezeedom experience.
I went to this delightful ice cream spot in Hoi An and was absolutely enchanted from the first scoop to the last. The customer service here is genuinely exceptional—what truly made my visit unforgettable was the gentle, lovely lady who warmly greeted me and took the time to chat.

Each scoop had this wonderfully playful, artisanal quality—you can tell these aren't just standard flavors but carefully crafted experiences. The textures were silky, the tastes were vibrant and balanced, and there was a genuine sense of creativity in every bite.

What could have been a quick dessert stop turned into one of the highlights of my trip, thanks to both the extraordinary ice cream and the heartfelt hospitality. If you're in Hoi An, do yourself a favor and visit this gem. Come for the whimsical flavors, stay for the warm, personal touch. I'll definitely be back!

p.s: I ate mango and passion fruit ice cream (vegan) and jaggery dark choco (with authentic Vietnamese chocolate).

A definite must try!!!

We had key lime cheesecake, candied hazelnut salted caramel, honeycomb and rum raisin. They were all so good. A definite must try!!! If you like nuts and a slight saltiness to the sweet, try the hazelnut. We actually wanted to try the tiramisu but it is soooo sold out. Quite a lot were but these that were had were amazing!!! Such good quality and they put in so much thought and attention to detail. In every cup!!!

The staff are super friendly and lovely! This is a local handcrafted ice cream shop, so there are plenty of flavors to choose from. I especially love the fruity ones like plum cider and MC  — try them with salted!! Trust me, it's an amazing combo. Yah definitely worth a try!

trip_context: {"Order type": "Dine in", "Meal type": "Other", "Price per person": "₫1–100,000"}
text: The best ice cream spot in Hoi An for sure and I’m glad I found the spot. The tiramisu ice cream was amazing. Art and feel of the shop was great and lastly the person who served us with the cool tattoos was the nicest person as well as another lovely waiter I met who is also a chef. It gives a comforting feel and I hope to be back again the next time I’m in Vietnam.

I had the keylime cheesecake and young coconut ice creams and they were delish. Their selections are interesting and I'd love to come back to try more. Alex, the lady who assisted us, was lovely and welcoming. They have an ice cream jenga in the shop which was fun to play with. Highly recommended!
Very good icecream with a lot of interesting flavours! The staffmember we met was so kind and attentive!!! We will come back

This is the best ice cream I have ever tried! 🍦
The café in Hoi An makes handmade ice cream using only natural ingredients – no artificial colors or added sugar, just pure flavor. There is a huge variety of flavors: from fresh and slightly tangy to rich and sweet.

The highlight is the owner herself. She explains each flavor with so much care: what it’s made of, what it will taste like, whether it’s more on the sweet side or has a refreshing tang. Every detail is described so clearly and with love for her craft.

The staff are incredibly friendly, and the atmosphere is warm and welcoming. This place definitely deserves not just 5, but 10 stars ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐.

Highly recommended to anyone visiting Hoi An – you won’t regret it!
They had so many flavors to choose from, and the server Alex was so kind. The ice cream was really good as well. I got the mangosteen and soursop sorbet, and it was absolutely delightful!
owner_reply:
Hi Sasha, thank you so much for your kind words! We’re really happy to hear you enjoyed the MC sorbet and had a great experience with Alex. We'll be sure to pass along your compliment.

The Mangosteen & Soursop sorbet is one of our favorite seasonal flavor as well, and we’re glad it hit the spot for you. Hope to welcome you back soon to hangout and try even more flavors!

With love,
Freezedom Team

place: Cơm Gà Cô MỲ - Co MY Chicken Rice
text:
A local gem for chiken rice lovers! 🍗🍚

We ate at Cơm Gà Cô MỲ and it was a treat from start to finish. The chicken rice was absolutely delicious: the chicken was tender and flavorful, the rice was perfectly seasoned, and everything was just right.

The place has a real local atmosphere, no frills, with a friendly and authentic vibe. You eat on small chairs in a simple but very pleasant setting.

The staff are super friendly, smiling and welcoming—you can feel their genuine passion for cooking and desire to please.
Excellent value for money and a genuine Vietnamese culinary experience.

I recommend it 100% if you're in the area!

text: I saw this little chicken and rice stand with a little row of seating down the alley.  I just love little gems like this serving great local dishes out in the outdoors.  This place must be a stop of local street food because I could overhear local foodie guides explaining things to the people their were with :).  The food was fresh....rice wasn't overcooked and the chicken was great.  The owner pointed out to squeeze a lime over top, put some chili sauce on top, and good covering of soya sauce.  Very tasty plate of food for $1.50 Canadian....25000VND.  You can tell the owners take pride in their food and we're very happy when I gave them the thumbs up 👍😀.

place: Cơm Gà Cô MỲ - Co MY Chicken Rice
text: Was the only foreign person eating there. Locals flock this spot to eat in or order for takeaway. The people who run this cart are very friendly and accommodating too, even prepared the dish with the correct seasonings after serving it. Great value comfort food, must try in Hoi An

place: Cơm Gà Cô MỲ - Co MY Chicken Rice
text: If you don't look out for the name on its food cart, you might miss it. Owners are a friendly husband and wife team. We came about half hour after they had opened, so it was quiet but the chicken rice was amazingly fresh. The chicken intestine/offal side that came with it was really tasty and well seasoned. The rice was also really light that it didnt make you feel heavy, and we could've easily went for a second plate. Great price for a banger meal.

place: Cơm Gà Cô MỲ - Co MY Chicken Rice
text:
The Com Ga is AMAZING. So amazing that we ordered one servicing then got a second one. Com Ga is chicken and rice that is served with herbs and salad. They also give you broth on the side and have limes and chilis to add to your dish.

It was 30k for 1 serving which was some of the most affordable food we’ve had in Hoi An.

I will be thinking about this meal for a while and will have to resort to attempting to recreate it at home since I’m leaving Vietnam soon.

text: I was recommended this restaurant by a local, one of three located right on the Con Toc ferry terminal - Tam Giang Lagoon. The restaurant is spacious, and a plus is that the owners are very enthusiastic, polite, and cheerful. It's newly opened, so it mainly attracts locals; tourists aren't yet familiar with it. However, I found the prices here to be reasonable, as I've eaten at the last branch I visited. They have a tank of fresh seafood for you to choose from. The dishes are served quickly and are attractively presented. My favorites were the Herring Salad and the Pickled Seaweed Salad. The crab with roe and green prawns are guaranteed to be delicious. One drawback is that the service is a bit slow, probably because the staff are new. Overall, it's definitely worth trying. The prices are reasonable for my budget.

text:
After being recommended by our hotel, we decided to try this restaurant—just note that it’s located upstairs above another restaurant, so it can be a little easy to miss.

They offer both Vietnamese and Western food, but we stuck with the Vietnamese options. It’s located right opposite a nightclub, which actually made for some pretty entertaining people-watching while we dined. You can choose to sit outside or downstairs in air conditioning.

We started with the papaya salad, which was very good—served with peanuts and dried onions—though not quite as fresh as what we experienced during a cooking class in Hoi An. The standout dish was definitely the eggplant with garlic and butter—absolutely amazing and a must-order.

We also had the beef hot pot, which came with very rare slices of beef that you cook yourself, along with vegetables and rice noodles. It was a fun and interactive meal.

Overall, a really nice experience, and great value at around 350,000.

trip_context: {"Order type": "Dine in", "Meal type": "Dinner", "Price per person": "₫1–100,000", "Noise level": "Moderate noise", "Parking space": "Difficult to find parking", "Parking options": "Free street parking"}
text:
Bánh Mì Chu Văn An is an absolute must-visit if you want to experience what a real Vietnamese bánh mì should taste like. It’s a small, humble street stall — nothing fancy at all — but what comes out of that tiny setup is pure perfection.
I ordered the special bánh mì, and honestly, it was the best bánh mì I’ve ever had. It comes loaded with everything — different types of meats, pate, pickled vegetables, herbs, sauces — and the combination is just brutal. Every bite is perfectly balanced: crunchy bread, rich and savory fillings, and that signature mix of sweet, salty, and slightly tangy flavors that make Vietnamese sandwiches so unique.
The bread was perfectly toasted — light and crisp on the outside, soft and warm inside — and it held together beautifully without falling apart, even with all those delicious fillings. The ingredients were incredibly fresh, and the sauce tied everything together just right. You can tell this is made by someone who knows exactly what they’re doing.
The woman who runs the stall is one of the kindest and warmest people I’ve met while traveling in Vietnam. She was super friendly and welcoming, smiling the entire time and clearly proud of her food. Even though her English was limited, communication wasn’t a problem — her kindness said it all. You can feel the love and care she puts into every sandwich.
The price is also fantastic — incredibly cheap for the quality and size of the sandwich. It’s one of those meals that makes you stop and think, “How can something this good cost so little?” You could easily pay three times as much elsewhere and not come close to this level of flavor or satisfaction.
What I loved most was that this isn’t a tourist trap — it’s a genuine, local spot serving real food for real people. There’s no marketing gimmick, no fancy decor — just honest, homemade perfection.
If you only have time to try one bánh mì while in Vietnam, make it this one. The special is the way to go — it’s got a little bit of everything, and the combination is absolutely spot-on.
The location is easy to find, and even if you have to wait a few minutes during busy hours, it’s completely worth it. Everything is made fresh, right in front of you, and the result is unforgettable.
Overall, Bánh Mì Chu Văn An is everything you want in a Vietnamese street-food experience: incredible flavor, friendly people, and unbeatable value. The special bánh mì is out of this world — truly the best I’ve had anywhere.

text:
A relaxing experience

As the name suggests, the cafe is located inside the famous Vi Da Hamlet. It is roomier than it looks with the backyard right next to the river, which offers a great view and calm asmotsphere.

I order one salted coffee and a set of imperial tea.

The coffee is great. The sweetness and saltiness of the cream complement the bitterness of the coffee, resulting in a sophisticated and well-rounded flavour profile.

Next is the tea set.
For an affordable price, this is one of the best tea experiences you can find. The brew features dried fruits and is served with a side of sweets to complement the flavors. Each sip offers a subtle bitterness and sweet aftertaste that finishes with a fragant herbal notes.

Last but not least, the employees are super friendly who carefully attend to your needs.

trip_context: {"Meal type": "Lunch"}
text:
If you are looking for the absolute best food in Vietnam, look no further than Nina’s Cafe. We came in for a late brunch that effortlessly turned into a long, delicious lunch—and honestly, we didn’t want to leave. After three weeks of traveling through the country, this was hands-down the best food and selection we’ve encountered.
​The atmosphere is incredibly relaxing and cozy, providing the perfect escape from the bustle of the city. However, what truly elevates this experience from a great meal to an unforgettable one is the hospitality. Our host, Ms. Lotus, was perfection. Her English is impeccable, and she is so much more than just a host; she is a cultural ambassador. She took the time to sit with us and educate us on the traditional way to prepare and eat each dish, adding a layer of depth to the meal that you just don't find elsewhere.
​We will be back again for sure. If you’re in Hue, do yourself a favor and find this hidden gem!

trip_context: {"Meal type": "Lunch", "Price per person": "₫100–200K", "Reservation": "Reservations not required", "Noise level": "Very quiet"}
text:
Finding Nina’s Cafe at the end of a long, quiet alleyway is half the fun—the other half is the incredible food and hospitality. This small, cozy spot is a peaceful escape from the main streets.

​The Service:
Huge shoutout to Lotus, who was a total powerhouse. She was the only server managing the entire restaurant single-handedly, yet she stayed welcoming, spoke excellent English, and took a genuine interest in our trip. Her recommendations were spot-on.

​The Standout Dishes:
​The BBQ Pork Noodles (Bun Thit Nuong): The pork had a fantastic flavor that reminded me of Filipino tocino, and the peanut sauce was the perfect finishing touch.

​Set 1: An absolute steal for the price. The Banh Beo was incredibly fresh, and the Banh Nam was a delicious highlight I’m glad we tried.

​Fried Fish: Light, crispy, and perfectly battered. It let the quality of the fish shine through instead of overpowering it.
​Grilled Lemon Chicken: This was "booming" with flavor—a massive hit with my son.

​If you want an authentic, quiet meal with top-tier service, make sure you find your way down the alley to this gem.

Nina’s café is a true gem, tucked away in a narrow street in central Hué. Do not hesitate to visit. The place feels fresh and welcoming, creating a lovely atmosphere from the moment you arrive.

Moon and N were extremely friendly and helped us choose our dishes with great care. They also speak excellent English, which is not always the case in many restaurants and cafés in Hué.

The food itself was delicious, beautifully presented, and very reasonably priced. The drinks were equally impressive, with great attention to detail in their presentation.

Highly recommended ☺️

Ngan our waitress was always with a smile and extremely kind.
If you are in Hue do not hesitate and eat there.

I love the lemongrass chicken on bamboo. It comes entirely in breast chicken meat. The gravy goes well with the white rice and I can request the kitchen to make the dish to be less spicy. The mushroom tofu claypot is also in my liking. It’s sweet and the sauce is great with rice. These two dishes are recommended.

The staff speaks English and makes recommendations. So, you would be taken care of if you are unfamiliar with the local food.

text:
Best meal we’ve had in Vietnam! After being disappointed by overpriced “fine dining” at other luxury resorts—where the food and atmosphere fell far below expectations, we decided to try Le Parfum at Azerai Hue. Knowing the hotel is owned by Adrian Zecha, the founder of Aman Resorts, we anticipated something special, and it delivered beyond our expectations.

The lamb rack was perfectly cooked and packed with flavor, the duck breast was tender and delicious, and the dessert trilogy crème brûlée was a unique treat with durian, hibiscus, and coffee flavors, all executed to perfection. text:
Family Home Café & Restaurant was one of those happy discoveries in Hue that turned into a genuine favourite. We ended up eating here several times during our stay, which really says it all. When a place pulls you back that consistently, it's doing something right.
The pho is wonderful — comforting, well-balanced, and exactly what you want after a day of exploring. But what surprised us was the shakshuka. Rich, flavourful, and totally unexpected on a Vietnamese café menu — it works brilliantly and we'd order it every time. Pair either with a cold beer in that cozy, relaxed setting and you've got yourself a near-perfect meal.
The atmosphere is warm and unpretentious, the kind of place that feels lived-in and welcoming rather than curated for tourists. It's easy to linger here, and we did — often. The staff play a big part in that. They're genuinely lovely, attentive without being intrusive, and add to the overall feeling that this is a place run with real care.
If you're spending time in Hue, put Family Home on your list early — that way you'll have plenty of chances to go back. Five stars without hesitation.

text:
Buddhist vegetarians who abstain from the five pungent spices (ngũ vị tân, e.g. onion, garlic, etc.) would love this place! Although the restaurant does serve food with the five pungent spices, the restaurant owner, Tạo, is a practicing Buddhist and perfectly understands this dietary requirement. He speaks good English and can advise you on which dishes can be made without the five pungent spices. We've dined in once and have been ordering in from him. text:
If you arrive in Huế by train, you might easily walk past this small and very unassuming place, but that would be a mistake. Mr Pho’s Pho and Cafe looks simple at first glance: plastic chairs, plastic tables, exactly what you would expect from a typical local Vietnamese spot. But behind that simplicity is truly great food.

The fried rice and fried noodles are excellent, fresh, flavorful, and perfect after a long journey. The prices are also very fair.

What really makes this place special, though, is Mr Pho himself. He takes great care of his guests, helps with train connections, gives travel tips, and if he has a moment, he even shares a few stories. You don’t feel like a customer there, you feel like a welcome guest.

It’s also very convenient for travelers: he offers to prepare food for your train journey and can store your luggage if you need to kill some time before your next train.

A genuine and authentic spot right next to the train station in Huế. Anyone passing through should definitely stop by.
★★★★★

text:
One of the BEST local food experiences we had in Hue! 🇻🇳❤️

Vietnamese Food - Hue Local Food & FastFood 22 Restaurant is honestly one of the best restaurants we found during our trip to Hue. It is located right in front of the Hue Imperial City, so it’s also a very convenient place to stop by while sightseeing.

We came here almost immediately after arriving in Hue, and we were so impressed that we already feel like we’ve found our “hidden gem” in Hue!

The owner was incredibly kind and welcoming, and the restaurant has cool air conditioning, which was such a relief after walking around in the hot and humid weather. Most importantly, every dish we ordered was delicious and tasted fresh and authentic.

We ordered Bún Bò Huế, Morning Glory, Bánh Cái, Bánh Nậm, a mango smoothie, and watermelon juice.

The little touches made the experience even better. We only ordered the Morning Glory, but they kindly gave us rice for free, and complimentary wet tissues were also provided.

And just when we thought we were finished and were about to leave, the owner surprised us with complimentary passion fruit and ginger tea as dessert! 🥭🍵

The food was delicious, the service was warm and genuinely friendly, the restaurant was clean and comfortable, and the prices were very reasonable.

If you're visiting Hue and want to try authentic local Vietnamese food in a comfortable, welcoming restaurant, I highly recommend stopping here.

We came in simply looking for a meal, but we left feeling like we had discovered a place we would happily come back to again.

If you're in Hue, put this restaurant on your list! You won't regret it. 👍👍👍👍👍

⭐ Delicious food
⭐ Friendly owner
⭐ Great value
⭐ Air-conditioned & comfortable
⭐ Generous complimentary extras
⭐ Perfect location near the Imperial City

Highly recommended! 🇻🇳❤️

text:
I wish I had found this place on my last trip, but was super stoked to have found it on this trip to Hue.

The restaurant is set up in a garden with tables set up around it as well.

We started off sitting in the garden but there were some mosquitos so we moved away from the lush garden setting. Probably something that's hard to get away from as the weather warms up.

We ordered several platters with many things to try. One of my favorites was from "Hue on a Tray" where three different "banh" were offered. The black sesame item was exceptional both in taste and texture.

We also ordered the "Traditional Hue Meal" which included rice, veggies, tofu, soup, and a very unique pickled eggplant dish.

The Pomelo Salad was also very tasty.

I suggest making a reservation as the restaurant, though not full, was rather busy on a weeknight.

text:
Incredibly peaceful vegetarian/vegan garden refuge in the middle of Hue. The moment u walk in, you are greeted by hanging orchids, beautiful paintings, statue-adorned zen garden pathways, accompanied by the relaxing sound of water, leaves rustling, and birds singing along with cicadas. It's literally another world.

The staff was honest, polite & knowledgeable, so much that my aunt wanted to adopt one of them.

Although they are mostly vegan, some dishes may have milk, so make sure you ask the staff first. We were told everything on the menu can be made vegan. If you let them know first, they will not add dairy.

The food was amazing, well-presented & full of flavor even tho they emphasize the health aspect of food. Everything was freshly prepared with minimal processing.

If u happen to stop by Hue, pls visit An Nhien Garden to rest and enjoy incredible food.

text:
The oldest temple in Da Nang, Tam Thai Temple was built around 1630 by monk Hung Lien, who came from China as a monk during the late Le Dynasty.
Among the legends surrounding Tam Thai Temple, the most frequently mentioned is the story of Emperor Nguyen Anh. While being pursued by the Tay Son army, Emperor Nguyen Anh fled to an island off the East Sea.
After a while, he returned and chose Ngu Hanh Son Mountain as his refuge, praying to Buddha that if he could defeat the Tay Son army, he would definitely restore this temple. After ascending to the throne, he ordered Emperor Minh Mang to restore the temple on his own site.
Later, in 1825, during the reign of Emperor Minh Mang, the temple was restored.
This ancient temple is over 400 years old and has unique and ancient architecture.
It is an ideal place to worship and enjoy the beautiful scenery at the temple.
Especially in the morning, the silence and piety will be more intense.
Beautiful, peaceful place where the sound of the monks praying echoed across the grounds. We we were there at night and the colours were spectacular.

Visiting Da Nang Museum is a new chapter of museum architecture and exhibition display in quality, design and arrangement in Vietnam. Similar improvements and developments are seen at the new military museum in Hanoi!
In Danang the contemporary architecture combines gently the old municipal villas with a modern annex that offers spacious rooms for the exhibition. The alignment of exhibition from colonial times, then American war till traditional ceramic and provincial minority cultures respects the artifacts and provide information mostly bilingual in Vietnamese and English. I would recommend that the video presentations have bilingual subtitles as well. Besides that visitors get a good insight about the Danang area and history. I personally find a more reflective information about the four wars that fought Vietnam for independence very interesting (against French, American, China and Cambodia). That would sum up that history background and provides with information that kept Vietnam in warfare for 40 years from that to recover the country is still working on. Finally, the museum is a great asset for the city! Congrats and kudos!

There was, I should mention, a special quality about this place. It felt atmospheric, surreal, and almost otherworldly. After spending some time there, I felt as though I had become a part of it.

trip_context: {"Visited on": "Weekday", "Wait time": "No wait", "Reservation recommended": "Yes"}
text:
The Da Nang Museum of Cham Sculpture is a great place to learn more about Cham culture. The Cham Kingdom was an ancient Hindu and Buddhist kingdom that was eventually weakened and integrated into Vietnam.

Entrance tickets are available on many travel platforms, and even via Google Maps. The price was great value for money. Visitors are mostly locals, although I did bump into a few expats during my visit.

The museum's main entrance faces the main road, close to Dragon Bridge. The building itself is an antique structure—I understand it was built by the French nearly a century ago. Therefore, it does not have air conditioning, which made it very hot during summer. Arriving early to avoid the heat is always advisable.

By logging into the museum’s Wi-Fi and going to their website, you can access the audio guide, which provides tremendous help in understanding the exhibits. Unfortunately, it was very difficult to log into the Wi-Fi, and I couldn't find the password either. Some locals helped me, but then I got a 403 Access Denied message because I had a VPN active on my phone. It took nearly 30 minutes to access the audio system, with the help of Gemini. In any event, there are guided tours as well.

The exhibits are amazing. One can see that the Cham Kingdom was deeply influenced by Hinduism and Buddhism. The exhibits include a lot of Buddha sculptures and various Hindu gods. The saddest thing to me was that many exhibits are heavily damaged, probably due to past changes in power. This phenomenon is not uncommon, especially in China.

There is a small cafe stall inside the museum. Alternatively, there is a nearby McDonald's, where I just refuelled with an iced coffee and an ice cream after the visit at a very reasonable price and rested for a couple of hours before moving on to the next spot.

place: Da Nang Museum of Cham Sculpture
trip_context: {"Visited on": "Weekday", "Wait time": "No wait", "Reservation recommended": "No"}
text:
One of the most impressive museums in Da Nang and truly one of the best museums I have visited anywhere. The collection of Cham sculptures and temple elements feels so significant that the museum itself reminds me of a UNESCO heritage site.

The staff here are incredibly kind and passionate. When I told them how interested I was in Cham culture, they even found a book in Russian and helped me learn more about the history and mythology of the Cham civilization. That level of care made the visit very special.

The exhibition is beautifully organized. As you walk through the halls you can see how the space is structured almost like a spiritual journey — with guardian figures such as Yakshas and Dvarapalas watching over the halls with the deities. Deeper inside, you encounter what feel like real temple remains and architectural fragments, reminiscent of places like Angkor Wat.

The museum preserves such a powerful sense of history that you can spend a long time quietly observing each sculpture. I spent almost an entire day here and learned so much.

The only thing I would suggest is adding a little more information about the early formation of the Cham dynasty, especially in the first hall where the map is displayed. A short article or QR code with additional historical context could make the experience even richer for visitors.

Thank you for preserving this beautiful and important culture and sharing it with the world. This museum is absolutely a must-visit in Da Nang.

Tip for visitors: plan at least 2–3 hours for this museum. If you are interested in history, mythology, or archaeology, you could easily spend half a day here.

Highly recommend visiting in the morning when it is quieter — it gives you time to really appreciate the sculptures and the atmosphere of the museum.
