Wandered through the upper French Village zone, taking in the European-style plazas, spires, and castle courtyards.

The Breakdown:

• SCENERY & ARCHITECTURE: Highly detailed mock-European medieval village featuring ornate spires, grand courtyards, cobblestone lanes, and striking marble interiors. Visually impressive for photography, with endless architectural angles spread across shifting terrace elevations.

• VIBE & DENSITY: The central fountain and church squares see high visitor concentration, but stepping into the peripheral side alleys and elevated viewpoints reveals quiet, almost desolate pockets with cool mountain breezes.

• PRACTICAL TIPS: Navigating the uneven stone steps and ramps requires sensible footwear, especially if moisture rolls off the ridges and slicks the paving stones.

Takeaway: An elaborate mountaintop architectural installation offering fantastic photography angles and relaxed alley strolls away from the main transit paths.

A place to admire the entire Son Tra Peninsula in Da Nang. The Son Tra Peninsula is a "precious gem" of Da Nang, considered the city's green lung that regulates the climate. Located about 10km northeast of Da Nang city center, the peninsula has a unique location with three sides bordered by the sea and one side bordered by the city, creating a unique natural forest ecosystem connected to the sea in Vietnam.

Key features of the Son Tra Peninsula:
* Strategic location: Known as the "eye of Indochina" during the resistance war due to its strategic observation role. This peninsula also acts as a natural barrier protecting against wind and storms and regulating the climate for Da Nang.

* Diverse ecosystem: Son Tra is a place where the typical flora and fauna of both North and South Vietnam intersect.

* Vegetation: Nearly 4,000 hectares of forest, with over 1,000 species of higher plants, including many large trees and valuable medicinal plants. In particular, there is a thousand-year-old banyan tree with a large trunk circumference and a massive root system, creating an impressive landscape.

* Wildlife: It is home to more than 366 animal species, including more than 43 rare species listed in the Vietnam Red Book and the International Red List (IUCN). The symbol of Son Tra is the brown-footed langur, a rare primate known as the "queen of primates". In addition, there are many diverse species of insects, birds, and reptiles.

* Marine ecosystem: The coastal waters of Son Tra are also very diverse with more than 100 species of seaweed and beautiful coral reefs, attractive for scuba diving and exploration.

* Nature Reserve: In 1992, the Son Tra forest reserve was officially recognized as the Son Tra Peninsula Nature Reserve. This is the only nature reserve located within the city limits of a major city in Vietnam.

Attractions on Son Tra Peninsula
Son Tra Peninsula offers a variety of experiences for visitors, from exploring nature to visiting spiritual sites:
* Linh Ung Pagoda at Bai But: A large pagoda with a 67m-tall statue of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara facing the East Sea, a famous spiritual tourist destination and a place where visitors can admire the panoramic view of Da Nang city from above.

* Ban Co Peak: The highest point on the peninsula, associated with the legend of the immortal playing chess. From here, you can gaze out over the entire city of Da Nang, the sea, and the majestic mountains.

* Thousand-Year-Old Banyan Tree: One of the highlights of Son Tra, with the ancient and majestic beauty of an "old banyan tree" that has existed for hundreds of years.

* Son Tra Lighthouse (Tien Sa Lighthouse): Built during the French colonial period, it is not only a lighthouse to guide ships but also an ideal check-in spot with a view of the vast blue sea.

* Pristine beaches: But Beach, Tien Sa Beach, Da Den Beach, Nam Beach... all possess unspoiled beauty, clear blue water, suitable for swimming, fishing, and picnicking.

* Bang Cliff: Distinguished by its unique black rock formations, it's an ideal place for sightseeing and photography.

* Tien Sa Port: An important seaport in Da Nang, welcoming many international cruise ships.

* Tien Sa Eco-tourism Area: Offering a blend of nature and modern amenities, with many outdoor activities.

* Oc Peak: The highest point of the peninsula, nearly 700m.

Potential and Challenges
Son Tra Peninsula has great potential for developing eco-tourism, resort tourism, and spiritual and cultural tourism. However, tourism development must go hand in hand with strict conservation efforts to protect the diverse ecosystem and precious natural landscape of Da Nang's "green lung". Managing investment projects and tourism activities to avoid negative environmental impacts is a major challenge that is receiving attention.

We went very much thinking that it would just be an activity for the kids but we ended up really enjoying it too. We got so much help and support and everyone really enjoyed the whole process. We were given space to take our time but also help when we needed it and it feels so special to have such a meaningful souvenir to bring home. Really glad we found such a great workshop! Thank you!

We went to the lantern lady without a booking and they managed to fit in my partner and I without any problems (Sunday afternoon). We both made our lanterns from the first step of building the frame and the staff carefully helped us at each part. We spent some time there and we are very happy with our lanterns! They are collapsible so we are able to take them with us on our travels. It's a lovely relaxing environment down a side street and the staff are warm and welcoming. I would highly recommend going to Lantern Lady!

With lanterns lighting up every corner of Hoi An, it’s tempting to just buy one and move on, but this experience lets you actually be part of it.

The staff were incredibly attentive and genuinely helpful. If you made a mistake, they didn’t just fix it for you, they showed you how to do it properly, which made the whole thing feel much more authentic. They guided us through each step without hovering, and were friendly the entire time.

You can customise everything - the shape, size, and fabric. You can either work with a pre-made frame or build the frame yourself if you want the full experience. Best part, the lanterns fold down to roughly the size of a drink bottle, so they’re easy to carry around all day or pack in your luggage.

Honestly considering going back for another one.

text:
🌊 Cham Island – A Green Corner of Nature and People 🌿

I've had the chance to visit Cham Island many times, and each time I've returned feeling relaxed and refreshed, like being "recharged" amidst pristine nature. It's an ideal place to learn about the island's marine ecosystem – from coral reefs and seagrass beds to unique marine life.

🌱 What I appreciate most is the local people's awareness of environmental protection and ecological conservation. They say no to plastic bags, minimize plastic waste, and constantly remind visitors to maintain cleanliness – something not every tourist destination achieves.

However, regarding the service organization, I think there should be more innovation and professionalism. Almost every tour only stops at: the exhibition area, the freshwater well, and Hai Tang Pagoda – places worth visiting, but which feel repetitive after multiple visits.

🌤 The morning sun was quite strong, and the range of activities wasn't very diverse. If there were more activities like a series of floating platforms on the sea, or a coconut water stand like a small beach bar, it would definitely attract more visitors – especially young people who love taking photos and enjoy fresh, vibrant experiences.

🇻🇳 But regardless, Cu Lao Cham remains an integral part of our homeland – simple, welcoming, and very Vietnamese. If you haven't been there, come once to understand why it's called "the green pearl in the middle of the Central Vietnamese sea."

We had such a fantastic experience here and would highly recommend it to anyone visiting Hoi An.

We chose to visit at 1pm, which turned out to be perfect as it was the hottest part of the day. The workshop is fully air-conditioned, with cold drinks available to buy from the fridge, making it a brilliant way to escape the heat while doing something memorable.

We came as a family with our 4-year-old daughter and grandparents, and it was an activity that everyone could enjoy together. The ladies running the workshop were incredibly patient, kind and encouraging, taking the time to demonstrate every step and helping whenever we got stuck without ever making us feel rushed. They were especially wonderful with our daughter, making sure she was involved throughout, guiding her carefully at every stage and ensuring she was progressing and enjoying herself the whole time. It really made the experience feel inclusive for all ages.

There are two workshop options:
• A 45–60 minute session where you decorate a pre-made lantern frame with your chosen fabric.
• A 90-minute session where you build the bamboo lantern frame yourself before covering it with fabric.

There is a huge selection of beautiful fabrics to choose from, so every lantern feels unique.

One of the best features is that the lanterns are designed to collapse flat, so you can easily pack them into your suitcase and take home a beautiful handmade lantern.

This was one of our favourite activities in Hoi An: relaxing, creative, suitable for all ages, and a lovely way to spend a few hours together as a family. If you’re looking for something different from sightseeing, don’t miss this experience!

text:
Onya Bike Tours – A Journey of a Lifetime

Touring Vietnam by motorcycle has been one of the greatest experiences of our lives.

From day one, we were warmly welcomed and thoroughly briefed on what to expect over the next seven days. The presentation was led by our group leader, Minh, along with his mechanic, Phong.

Our group of six riders ranged in age from our mid-30s to our late 60s, with varying levels of riding experience. Minh immediately put everyone at ease, assuring us that each rider would be capable of navigating every stage of the tour, while making it clear that safety was always his number one priority.

During the orientation, we were given a clear overview of each day’s ride while still leaving a few surprises for us to discover along the way. The evening before departure, we were fitted with our riding gear and provided with dry bags, bungee cords, and rain gear.

On the morning of departure, we inspected our motorcycles with the staff before setting off. At the end of every day, the bikes were checked, serviced, and prepared for the next day’s adventure, giving us complete confidence in the equipment.

The true highlight of this journey was Minh’s extensive knowledge of Vietnam’s history. He shared fascinating stories and insights into the country’s struggles, resilience, and remarkable journey to where it is today. Every historical site we visited was followed by an engaging explanation that brought each location to life. His passion for his country was evident and added tremendous value to the experience.

The riding itself was exceptionally well planned. We experienced stunning mountain vistas, winding roads, incredibly twisty sections, and relaxed scenic touring. It truly was a motorcyclist’s dream.

We do have a few suggestions that we believe would make an already excellent tour even better while adding another layer of safety:

* Equip the guides and riders with communication systems. Being connected to the guides—and to each other—would be especially valuable when navigating the busy and often chaotic traffic in the cities. At a minimum, both guides should have communication systems.
* Carry a small supply of miscellaneous repair items, such as visor hardware or basic helmet parts, to deal with minor equipment issues that can arise during a week-long tour.
* Replace some of the rain gear. Although it was worn correctly, several riders still became quite wet during heavy rain.
* Give guides the flexibility to recognize when a particular section of terrain may be beyond the comfort level of some riders and offer an alternate route when appropriate.
* Ensure the lead guide is equipped and trained to act as the initial responder should an emergency occur.

We also want to commend your entire team for the professionalism shown throughout the trip. The hotels were, in general, comfortable and well chosen. Minh consistently selected outstanding restaurants that showcased the unique flavours of each region while offering fresh, healthy, and authentic Vietnamese cuisine. Every meal was memorable.

Thank you to the entire Onya Bike Tours team for an unforgettable adventure.

On behalf of Paul, Gary, Nauris , Lauris, Brian, and Don—thank you for creating memories that will last a lifetime.

The area is a bit catered towards tourists, but still felt authentic to me. Especially after talking a bit with some of the people. They are super friendly.

If you want to explore a traditional craft village and learn more about the local culture in Hoi An, Kim Bong Carpentry Village is definitely a destination worth experiencing.
When I came here, I had the chance to learn about the traditional carpentry craft that has been preserved through many generations. What I enjoyed the most was seeing the artisans carve, engrave, and shape wooden products by hand. Each product shows the skill, care, and dedication of the craftsmen. 🪵🔨
The most interesting experience was getting to try making a simple wooden product by myself, feeling how challenging each step was and understanding more about the value of the traditional carpentry craft. It was not only a fun activity but also helped me appreciate more the cultural values preserved in this craft village.
The village is peaceful, rustic, and close to nature, giving a completely different feeling from the busy atmosphere of Hoi An Ancient Town.
It was an experience that was both interesting and meaningful, especially suitable for those who love culture, traditional handicrafts, and want to discover a more peaceful side of Hoi An.

text:
I’ve been to quite a few museums, and most of the time they feel very grand and formal, with all these beautiful pieces displayed with information about where they came from, what they mean, when they were made, etc.

But this little museum in Hoi An felt so different to me.

Everything felt so personal. The clothes, accessories and other pieces weren’t just there as exhibits. They were displayed together with photographs of the actual people and communities they came from, and Réhahn himself had met and photographed many of them during his travels around Vietnam.

Even the descriptions beside the pieces didn’t feel like the usual museum plaques. They felt more like little stories about the people, how he met them, and the places he visited.

I don’t really know how to explain it properly, but walking through the museum almost felt like I was there with him when he met these people. Looking at the photographs, especially their faces and their eyes, somehow made me feel like I had met them too.

Out of all the museums I’ve visited, I don’t think I’ve ever experienced one that felt this intimate and human. I’m honestly not even a very sentimental person, but there were moments walking around where I genuinely felt a little emotional.

Such a small art gallery museum, but probably one of the most memorable ones I’ve visited.
owner_reply:
We’re glad the personal stories alongside the photographs made your visit feel so close to the people represented. It means a great deal that you found time to pause with their faces and the objects connected to their lives. Thank you for spending that time with us.

The Réhahn Team

Unfortunately the area is quite littered and the seawater was murky during our visit. There isn’t much to see for snorkelers either, so I wouldn’t recommend it if you’re looking for marine life.

It’s best to bring your own drinks and snacks, as there is no facilities. Access to the beach is very easy and straightforward, making it a convenient stop if you’re exploring Cham Island.

One of the best beaches to relax, unwind and enjoy the sunset. The beach is clean and well-maintained, with plenty of sunbeds available. There’s also a restaurant and bar right on the beach.

Not the best spot for snorkeling, as the seabed is mostly sandy with little to see underwater. Keep an eye on your belongings, though, as monkeys sometimes come down to the beach and may try to grab your stuff!

text: A fantastic island, beautiful sand and water. The cuisine is delicious. I recommend getting lost there and straying a bit from the beaten tourist trail.

Perfect for relaxing all day =))) They have full services from food and drinks to snorkeling gear rental. The seawater is clear and shallower than other beaches, making it easier to swim, but there are fewer corals.

You have to pay 20,000 VND just to enter the beach, then another 50,000 VND for a sunbed. Despite that, the monkeys will probably still steal food from your backpack because many tourists ignore the rules and keep feeding them.
The beach and the water are polluted by the thousands of boats arriving at the shore every day. Many visitors get drunk on the beach, leaving behind piles of trash, while the bars blast loud music that drowns out what little nature remains.
This island left me genuinely saddened. It is a powerful example of how uncontrolled mass tourism can destroy a place that was once truly beautiful. Shame.

Great, clean, beautiful beach. Nice corals and many different fish. No bars or restaurants, so bring your own if you plan to stay there for a few hours.
Highly recommend the place for a chill time and nice snorkeling
Good for basic snorkelling. Occasional garbage floating in the water. Clean, white, soft sand and clear water. Some shade with a couple of swings. Easy access from main road

Very beautiful beach, the best on the island. Very white sand and some snorkelling, though visibility was low (2m) in the water and we did not see many corals ourselves.

No facilities like showers or chairs. Park on road with the locals and rest under the trees in the shade.

Best beach on the island. Pristine clear water, fine white sand, clean, and calm water. A little small but so beautiful. Watch out for rocks in the water! A little busy at night but that’s to be expected since this is the best beach and it’s near the pier.

Nice beach, also good for snorkeling:) There’s litter also in the sea, but you can help collecting them (you can always find bags to collect) and put it by the entrance (or next to the road) and they will take care of that. Some people just crying about the litter, but honestly you can also help the locals -it won’t disappear by itself.

This is the most beautiful island all over the country, for me.  This beach especially is calm with no rushing waves, white sand, and clear blue water, no benches for tourists, all so natural.  Most of all, not crowded. Find a shade under trees if you want to stay longer.  or just lie in the water.
Amazing small cove with a beautiful clean beach with soft white sand and clear waters! Lots of coral & small fishes. Had the beach all to myself, it was so peaceful!

We made a very early morning visit to one of the most important temples in Hoi An, the Chùa Pháp Bảo, a Mahayana temple. It is the headquarters of Hoi An’s Buddhist Association.

The flowers in the courtyard were exquisite; the elaborate landscaping here (and everywhere) is to celebrate Tet.

It was a lovely and peaceful time to visit. They were only two other people there praying.

trip_context: {"Visited on": "Weekday", "Wait time": "No wait", "Reservation recommended": "No"}
text:
This was the first significant stop on our morning walking tour of
Hoi An old town . The Phap Bao Pagoda, is located at 7 Hai Ba Trung Street in Hoi An.

On entering the grounds we were asked to don a light covering over our bare legs as a mark of respect.

The building and beautiful gardens are marvelous. It showcases traditional Vietnamese architecture with intricately carved wooden beams, majestic Buddha statues, and serene, colourful gardens.

The pagoda serves as a focal point for the local Buddhist community.

A lovely peaceful, shady place to escape the hub bub and heat of the town.

place: Minh Hien Vegetarian Cooking Class Tour
text:
This experience was the one of the highlights of our trip to Hoi An.

The chef-proprietor personally picked us up from our hotel and whisked us away to his restaurant where we were provided bikes.

After a relaxing and picturesque ride we reached the Tran Que Vegetable Village and the chef took us around the fields showing us all the herbs and how to identify them. Eating herbs straight off the farm was an absolutely delightful experience.

After that we cycled back to a market where one can purchase fresh vegetables. The chef helped us cool down with a great fruit smoothie and fabulous Hoi An pancake. Knowing that this was 100% vegetarian made the experience that much better.

Once cooled off we went around the market identifying different sellers and vegetables.

Post this, it was time for the cooking to begin which meant another short ride to the main restaurant.

It is an extremely nice setting in which to learn how to make 6 different dishes and some base sauces. One of the best aspects was that the chef not only made it seem easy but made you experience it as well. Which increases your confidence to replicate this for when you return back home.

After cooking we sat down to eat and all of it was incredible.

Highly recommend this experience.

place: Minh Hien Vegetarian Cooking Class Tour
text: Fantastic experience for all food lovers (not just vegetarians). Morning  started with an easy bike ride to an organic vegetable and herb farm. The class wS outstanding, easy to follow, lots of useful tips and great fun. The best part? Sitting down for a shared lunch with 6 delicious dishes we had just created. Great value at 900k VND

place: Minh Hien Vegetarian Cooking Class Tour

Normally this part is done by bike, but as we could not do this, the chef picked us up from our hotel with his car and drove us back and forth to the farm. After that we made a trip to a local market, where we got to try some local snacks and buy fresh ingredients for the class. Then we had the cooking class with delicious food, which we got to eat at the end of the class. We prepared 6 dishes. We learnt so much and will definitely be using the recipes, which the chef sent us by email, to cook at home! Definitely recommend this cooking class tour!!

text:
Absolutely stunning viewpoint overlooking the entire main village on Cham Island!
This spot is pure magic - you get a panoramic view of the whole village, the harbor, and the surrounding turquoise waters. Perfect for photos, especially at sunset or golden hour. The scenery feels wild and untouched, exactly why I love exploring Cham Island.

Pro tip: The road leading up here is quite steep and narrow with some sharp turns, so ride carefully on your scooter (especially if it's raining or you're not used to Vietnamese mountain roads). Take it slow, use low gear, and enjoy the ride - it's worth every bit of effort.

Highly recommend detouring here if you're on the island. One of the best free viewpoints around. Bring water and your camera!

If you are planning a trip to Hue, you absolutely must book David as your guide. We kicked off our first evening with an incredible culinary adventure, where his deep local roots allowed us to discover remarkable, hidden food spots that we never could have stumbled upon by ourselves. He completely looked after us, sharing wonderful insights into the culinary traditions of central Vietnam.
The following day, David led us on an exceptional city tour, completely bringing the area's majestic landmarks and rich historical heritage to life with his immense knowledge and infectious passion. He curated the perfect itinerary, ensuring we were never rushed and could truly absorb everything. With the added bonus of a spotless, air-conditioned car and a wonderful driver who prioritized our safety, every moment was effortless. text: Hoi An

We took the tour from Da Nang to Hoi an. It was so much fun. We got picked up at our hotel and dropped off at our next hotel in Hoi an. An absolute bucket list experience – I had a headache from smiling so much!
​If you are traveling between Hue and Hoi An, do yourself a massive favor and forget the bus or train. Booking a trip with the Lee Family Riders was hands down one of the best things we’ve ever done.
​We actually just randomly bumped into them while we were walking around the Citadel in Hue. Honestly, when they first pitched it to us, it felt a bit too good to be true. We were naturally pretty skeptical about a random happening like that on the street, but we decided to take the chance—and man, did it pay off!
​I opted to ride my own bike, while my wife sat passenger, and the setup was absolutely perfect for both of us. The coastal and mountain roads are spectacular, but what makes this tour so stress-free is how organized they are. You don’t have to worry about a thing—they take your big suitcases and transport them safely ahead of you, so you're completely free to just enjoy the freedom of the road.
​Also, quick tip for booking: they ask for payment via PayPal, which can sometimes make you hesitate with independent tours, but don't be put off by it at all. It is 100% legit.
​Cruising over the Hai Van Pass with the wind in your face and those insane coastal views is something we will never forget. The guides are absolute legends—incredibly safe, they know the roads like the back of their hand, and they keep the energy high the entire day. By the time we rolled into Hoi An, my face genuinely ached because I had a headache from smiling so much.
​An absolute 11/10 experience. If you get the chance, just do it!

place: Hue Touring - Mister T - Easy Rider - Adventure Motorbike Vietnam
text:
My husband booked the Hai Van Pass tour with Mr T Easy Rider and honestly, it was one of the best tours we’ve done in Vietnam.

We’d already visited the Marble Mountains on our last trip, so our driver changed the itinerary for us. We rode through the Hai Van Pass, stopped for a swim and lunch, and then went up to Ban Co Peak to watch the sunset. The views were amazing and the whole day was just brilliant.

place: Madam Tran Hue Cuisine - Cooking Class
text:
Seriously! 5/5 🌟!!
My son and I have been eating around Hue and he asked if we can find a cooking class for his favorite Hue dishes. Our concierge recommended Madam Tran’s class.
The class was done in her cute outside kitchen patio. We went in the middle of summer but her cooling unit kept us comfortable. She had all the ingredients prepped, introduced, mise en place…very clean kitchen. Both her husband, Tony and Thuy (Madam Tran) speak a bit of English so it made it easy for me. My Vietnamese is not that great! And the Hue dialect/accent throws me off.
Right from the start, we noticed everything is made from scratch, whole/fresh ingredients. She only uses packaged goods when the ingredient list is simple. Just her methods, secrets were worth the class! Hue style is much more savory and spicy (adjustable) than what I’ve learned growing up.
Three hours later…we had a full meal to taste our new skill and efforts. My son (15yo) took his first bite and he came out of his socks! If you have kids, when they love something…it brings joy to your heart. It was that moment for me. He said it was the best meal he’s had in VN EVER! And we’ve traveled from North to South. That meal was magical, home cooking certainly has a special place. I loved every bite!
What did we cook? My son requested; bánh beo, bánh xèo (khoai), bún thịt nướng, and nem lui.
They are a lovely couple, it was like we were invited to a friend’s home to have dinner for the evening. To that, I am stuffed and happy!

text:
The Hill (Bunker) in Hue is a hidden and unusual historical spot that combines Vietnam War history with beautiful natural scenery. Located on a quiet hill surrounded by trees, the site contains old military bunkers and offers peaceful views over the Perfume River and the surrounding landscape.

The biggest highlight is the atmosphere. Unlike the famous royal tombs and crowded tourist attractions in Hue, this place feels more raw and untouched. Walking around the old bunkers, sitting under the trees, and enjoying the view gives a feeling of stepping into a forgotten part of history.

The viewpoint is especially nice around sunset, when the river and countryside create a very calm and scenic atmosphere. It is also a good place for photography and for travelers who enjoy hidden places away from the usual tourist routes.

However, don’t expect a large museum or a fully developed attraction. The main value is the combination of history, nature, and the quiet feeling of the location. Some parts may feel simple and the site is more interesting for people who enjoy exploring rather than looking for many activities.

A great hidden gem in Hue for history lovers, photographers, couples, and anyone who wants to experience a more peaceful and different side of the city. Especially worth visiting together with Vong Canh Hill or nearby attractions.

Thuận An Beach, located just a short drive from the historic city of Huế, is a hidden gem along Vietnam’s central coast. Unlike the busier beaches further south, it offers a tranquil escape with soft golden sands stretching along the shoreline and gentle waves lapping at the shore. The beach is ideal for early morning strolls, sunrise photography, or simply soaking in the peaceful coastal atmosphere.

The surrounding area features local fishing villages, giving visitors a glimpse into the authentic daily life of Vietnamese coastal communities. Seafood here is fresh and plentiful, with small beachside eateries serving simple yet delicious dishes. The atmosphere remains relaxed even during weekends, making it a great spot for photographers seeking natural light, reflections in the water, and unobstructed horizon shots.

For travelers, Thuận An Beach is easily accessible by motorbike, taxi, or private car from Huế city center, and parking is straightforward. Facilities are modest but sufficient, including local stalls for refreshments and shaded areas to rest. The beach is also safe for swimming, with lifeguards present in certain sections during peak season.

Photographers will appreciate the wide-open spaces, scenic dunes, and occasional fishing boats that create compelling foregrounds. Sunrise and sunset provide excellent lighting conditions for capturing the serene beauty of the area, while the nearby lagoon adds variety to landscape compositions.

Overall, Thuận An Beach is a peaceful and photogenic coastal retreat that offers both natural beauty and cultural authenticity. It’s perfect for those looking to escape the crowds and enjoy a calm, scenic Vietnamese beach experience.

Free beach for tourist, nice view and you can meet alot of nice person.

Huế thương 😊 such a beautiful wild beach, hidden part of Hue

Not worth a visit at all. The road there is terrible, they’re building a highway bridge, it is muddy and overall not a good experience. The beach itself is not worth it either, there is nothing but a load of trash everywhere. Save yourself the effort and time.
Free beach about 15km away from Hue city, worth to try while you are in Hue.

We had a great morning with Nina. If you have the time, take a cooking class in the morning and don't miss out on the market tour. Nina explained how things work there and showed us all the different vegetables, fruit, candy etc. It was super interesting and Nina was a great guide. After that, we took a short walk to her restaurant for the cooking class. Again she took her time to explain every step in detail and so we easily managed to prepare four delicious dishes together. The spring rolls we made were the best we had on our whole trip to Vietnam and the Hué style pancake is a bomb! We even took food with us for a picknick later that day. We booked only one day in advance and could also shift time starting according to our needs. Thank you for the great class, Nina! (P.s.: Btw, Nina, we got the grater at the market on the next day at the same stand we bought the knife together on our tour ;)

We were thrilled to find Nina's Cooking class as we wanted to be able to replicate Vietnamese food at home. Nina took us to the market where she explained veges and we tasted fruit that we'd seen in our travels but didn't know how to eat it or didn't have the courage to try. We went to Nina's restaurant "Ba Tam" and had a great morning preparing and cooking a 4 course meal and Nina has sent us the recipes. We highly recommend this experience. By the way do not eat breakfast because you will be cooking a large feast. Thank you Nina and thank you to your lovely mother and staff.

Book this cooking class immediately! One of the best ones I have done. Nina is so kind and teaches you about the local market and how to cook various dishes. The food we cooked under her guidance was superb so make sure you bring an empty stomach and big appetite! The Banh Khoai and Bun Cha was delicious. It was lots of fun chatting with Nina whilst cooking and she helped us with some Vietnamese phrases too. 10/10 would recommend. 🥰

We booked the class at the last minute the night before, Nina was adorable and agreed to take us the next day.
She took us through the market, made us discover plenty of fruits and veggies.
The class was great, we had a great time, and the food was delicious!
We highly recommend!

We had an absolutely fantastic experience at this cooking class. The day started by going to the local market. We were able to try lots of new foods and the market itself was an amazing experience. We then went back to start our cooking . The class took place on a beautiful balcony, we were provided with refreshments and were able to help prepare all the ingredients for the cooking class with Nina and her colleague. Nina and her colleague were so kind and we really enjoyed spending the afternoon learning how to cook many Vietnamese dishes. At the end of the cooking class we ate on the balcony. We had so much food and Nina was so kind to box the leftovers up for us as we were taking a night bus. If you are in Hue I would 100% recommend this cooking class. It was one of our favourite things we did in Vietnam.

Nina was one of the most wonderful persons I met on my trip to Vietnam. She responded quickly to my request to arrange a lesson for the next day by doing everything she could to arrange it even though she had no other requests. In the end the lesson could not be arranged, but she still invited me to her restaurant (where I had a great meal). Despite a lot of work, she took the time to be with me and tell me about her cooking classes by which she perfects her recipes by mixing different culinary traditions. Everything she says and does conveys her enormous passion for cooking. I think anyone who wants to take an authentic cooking class should consider Nina's one.

Nina's cooking class is a must do experience. We organized it quite last minute but although she is very busy, she was very accommodating and arranged the class for the following morning.

We first went for a tour around the local market where she showed us many different types of fruits, vegetables and other foods. We also tried a delicious sweet bean dessert. We then walked to her restaurant to start the class.

First we were offered a refreshing drink of our choice - tea, fruit juice, smoothie etc, and cold water. The class was on the lovely balcony outdoors. We prepared 4 dishes - spring rolls, crispy Hue pancakes, fried aubergine with sauce, and chicken curry. It was very hands on and Nina talked us through each step.

The food was delicious and we learned a lot, I love this class because it was all things that would be easy to make at home regardless which country you are from. We then ate what we cooked - it was a huge spread!! We were so full, Nina kindly boxed up the rest of the food to take home.

She also brought us a big variety of fruits that we had seen at the market to try, including soursop, coc, mangostein, Longan, rambutan which were all delicious! And even some of these to take home too, along with spices and rice papers.

She also shared a lot with us about Vietnese culture and made us laugh! She is a lovely person and we couldn't recommend this class more highly. We wish you all the best and good luck with your business Nina.

Nina's cooking class was simply amazing! My expectations were exceeded by Nina's enthusiasm and love of her local food and city. I loved how Nina lets the customer choose what food off her menu they want to cook, and shares her passion in the kitchen while guiding us through each meal. With a trip to the market and an explanation about the different foods and way of doing things, Nina goes above and beyond for her fellow foodies. I will be returning to Nina's Cafe in the future and doing another cooking class. Do yourself a favor and go to Huể and say G'day to Nina, her family and friends and let them take you on an unforgettable foodies experience.

text: Must-visit for history lovers. The museum preserves a huge collection of royal artifacts in a stunning palace setting. It's clean, well-preserved, and offers a deep dive into Hue's imperial past. Since it's included in the main ticket, there's no reason to miss it. It's much more chill than the Forbidden City, allowing you to actually look at the details without being pushed by crowds.

peaceful here. nice gardens and some cool artefacts to see, although bear in mind they're mostly from 19th/20th c and all the Áo were replicas. if you walk around past the toilets there's a cool exhibition about one of the emperors and his family after his exile during the French occupation. 50,000 dong pp.

trip_context: {"Visited on": "Weekend", "Wait time": "No wait", "Reservation recommended": "Not sure"}
text:
The place itself is excellent and rich in Vietnamese culture and history. It’s definitely worth visiting to explore the beauty of the ancient kingdom and its heritage.
However, be very careful when you arrive, do not rent a rickshaw. We made that mistake and had a very disappointing experience. The drivers charged us 375,000 VND for one hour. Before renting, they showed us pictures of four places, but in reality, they only took us to two within that time. We followed our car driver’s suggestion, which unfortunately turned out to be the wrong decision.

In fact, the main palace is just a short walk from the entrance, and the entry ticket is only 200,000 VND. If you skip the rickshaw, you can save that extra money. Instead, the rickshaw drivers took us to a museum (50,000 VND per person) and even to irrelevant stops like a goldsmith shop, which wasted a lot of our time in the hot weather.
Because of this, we didn’t have enough time to enter the palace, which was the main reason for our visit. It honestly felt like a scam.
My advice: skip the rickshaw and walk directly to the palace.

trip_context: {"Visited on": "Weekday", "Wait time": "No wait", "Reservation recommended": "No"}
text:
The museum provides additional insight into the life of the king and the royal family. It covers what they went through, the impact they had on the city of Hue, and the king’s life in exile in France. There is also information about his daughter and his artwork.

The museum is not very large, but it is enough to spend one or two hours if you take your time. The entrance fee of 50,000 VND is very affordable.

Since the palace is nearby, it makes sense to visit it afterward.

The museum is dedicated to preserving and showcasing artifacts from the Nguyen Dynasty (1802-1945), Vietnam's last feudal dynasty. It holds a collection of nearly 10,000 antiquities that offer a glimpse into the daily life, rituals, and artistic talents of the royal court.

I had a meaningful visit to the Ho Chi Minh Museum in Hue. The museum is well organized and offers a fascinating insight into President Ho Chi Minh's life, legacy, and contributions to Vietnam's history. The exhibits are informative, and the historical artifacts are carefully preserved.

The atmosphere is peaceful, and the staff are friendly and helpful. I especially appreciated how the museum presents history in an engaging and respectful way, making it a worthwhile experience for visitors of all ages.

If you're interested in Vietnamese history and culture, the Ho Chi Minh Museum is definitely worth visiting. It's an educational and inspiring place that I would highly recommend.

Fake Alcohol- Excercise with caution!

Please be extremely careful if you choose to visit this establishment. Consider this a warning based on my experience.

I visited with friends and we ordered an Absolut vodka package, as it is typically our preferred drink. The drinks were brought to our table, and the server immediately opened the bottle and poured it into our glasses, mixing it with Coke for everyone except me, as I prefer mine over ice.

Upon taking my first sip, I experienced an intense burning sensation at the back of my throat that lasted for about a minute, followed by a sharp, unpleasant bitterness. Having consumed vodka on many occasions, I am confident in saying that what was served did not taste authentic.

Based on this experience, I strongly advise others to be cautious.

Helio Night Market is a fantastic choice for a family evening in Da Nang.

Both adults and kids will find something to love here. The market is clean, beautifully organized, and full of energy, with colorful lights, lively music, exciting fair-style games, and an incredible variety of delicious street food.

Children can enjoy the fun rides and games while adults relax, explore the food stalls, and soak up the vibrant atmosphere. Whether you’re looking for local specialties or international treats, there’s something for every taste. I loved wandering through the bustling stalls, trying different dishes. Helio is a fun place to spend an evening and experience Da Nang’s youthful, energetic spirit.

It’s the perfect place to laugh, eat, play, and create wonderful memories together. If you’re traveling with family, Helio Night Market is definitely a destination you shouldn’t miss.

A fantastic night market where you can enjoy not only a wide variety of food stalls but also live performances. It was great to grab some diverse food and enjoy the music performances on the stage. text:
This is my honest review given after being request by staff:

I came here on a weekend for a solo meal (without a reservation) after being told that were no free tables at the other restaurant/bar on the other floors, so I could watch the Dragon Bridge show - a great scenic view that avoids the crowds from the main road.

Fortunately, I did not need to wait long to be seated or for my orders to come. They play western pop music and love songs (English lyrics) out loud on big speakers. The menu given digitally on a touchscreen tablet rather than in print.

I ordered the seafood spring rolls and a lobster in Cajun style (spicy) as recommended by one of the servers; it was a locally-sourced spiny lobster species, quoted 600g (medium-sized apparently), pricing being by per 100g of weight, and it comes with sliced banh mi style bread. I'm not an expert on fine dining or eating seafood but the spring rolls were tiny compared to traditional cha gio/nem ran. The lobster was somewhat underwhelming because it seemed like not all its flesh was served on my plate. I also ordered a bottle of water and a tiger beer (330ml can) as well as a shisha pipe (apple, blueberry, mint flavour) which was massive to my surprise (reminded me of massive glass pipe for a special kind of 'herb').

Anyway, if you are coming here for a special occasion like a date or with family/friends, then it's good as there is definitely a romantic vibe. The servers are friendly especially Minh Tuan and Nhu Huyen; both guys endeavoured to accommodate me as a 'viet kieu' man with less-than-fluent Vietnamese - they provided an overall positive friendly service even though we needed to communicate via Google translate.

The food itself tastes good but it let down by its actual portion size. If you are sensitive to seafood and spiciness, take caution as you may feel unwell afterwards or in the folllowing morning. The prices are quite high too for what it is, so be warned. Essentially, you are paying for an unobstructed view of the Dragon Bridge, with nice vibes, unique location and picture-esque atmosphere. If you want to save money and feel like you're getting your money's worth, then order cheaper/fewer items as you'll save a lot more because the fancy luxuries come at a premium price.
owner_reply:

We take all feedback seriously and strive to improve the quality of our food and service. We hope to have the opportunity to welcome you again with a more fulfilling experience in the future.

text:
Vấn Cocktail Bar has a stylish, cosy interior with comfortable air conditioning and spotless facilities, including exceptionally clean restrooms, but the drinks and overall counter experience fell short.

Sitting at the counter, the hospitality felt quite distant. The bartenders and manager speak very limited English, making it tricky to discuss drink preferences or ask for recommendations. It felt as though eye contact was avoided until we actively flagged someone down, while local guests received much more attentive service.

The menu concepts look promising on paper, but the drinks lacked the complexity and strength expected at this price tier:

* Cacao: Described as one of their stronger options, but it tasted fairly mild and sweet. Decent enough, though nothing truly standout.
* Hoa Mạch: Ordered in search of a spirit forward cocktail. You get a subtle hint of the buckwheat, but the drink overall lacks body, depth, and spirit punch.
* Tomyum: Easy enough to drink and reasonably balanced, but quite standard.
* Canh Chua & Phở: Overpowered by intense chilli heat and spices. It hits you with immediate spice, but completely misses the rich, savoury, brothy depth you expect from a phở-inspired cocktail.

A major part of the craft speakeasy appeal is the bar theatre, seeing the bottles, watching the ratios, and observing how your drink is crafted. Here, most of the visible effort went into endlessly hand shaving ice, while the actual cocktail mixing happened out of sight and the drinks simply appeared. For a premium cocktail lounge in Da Nang, the execution across drink flavours and counter hospitality leaves noticeable room for improvement.

text:
As full-time travelers behind our Sunsets & Speakeasies YouTube channel, we’re always on the hunt for cocktail bars that offer something genuinely unique. Vặn Cocktail Bar instantly earned a place among our favorites in Da Nang. From the moody lighting and sophisticated design to the carefully curated music, everything about the space feels intentional. It’s the kind of cocktail bar you settle into for the evening rather than just stopping by for one drink.

Open for around three years, Vặn is home to an exceptionally talented team of mixologists who have created one of the most creative signature menus we’ve come across in Southeast Asia. Each cocktail draws inspiration from a different Southeast Asian country, blending regional flavors into drinks that are as visually stunning as they are delicious. Every cocktail arrived looking like a miniature work of art.

The staff were incredibly knowledgeable, taking the time to explain the inspiration and ingredients behind each drink while providing attentive service throughout the evening. It’s clear they’re passionate about their craft.

We love finding bars that tell a story through their menu, and Vặn does exactly that. As the evening went on, the atmosphere became even more vibrant, and it’s easy to see why the venue fills up after 10 p.m. We visited on a Saturday, when the live DJ added another layer of energy without taking away from the intimate, upscale vibe.

One quick tip: bring cash, as the bar is currently cash only.

If you appreciate exceptional cocktails, talented mixologists, and beautifully designed spaces, Vặn Cocktail Bar is an absolute must-visit in Da Nang. Between the artistic drinks, outstanding service, and unforgettable atmosphere, it’s a bar we’ll happily return to every time we’re back in the city.

Five stars without hesitation. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ 🍸✨🎶

text: I absolutely loved visiting Hue Walking Street. The area was a series of streets closed off to the usual traffic. In place, market stalls were set up along side the regular restaurants and souvenir shops. I was very lucky as I didn't realise it was only open on the weekend. I found the atmosphere to be very exciting and vibrant. Unlike some other walking streets I visited, this had a wholesome, family friendly appeal but also catered to wider audiences with bars and drinking venues. text: When you are looking for food and fun.  Check out Hue walking street on a Saturday or Sunday night.  Streets are closed on these nights from 6pm.  It becomes alive with loud music and people.  Lots of restaurants, shops, massages, mini marts, pharmacy and more.  Kids playing soccer (football) and badminton in the streets were a  highlight.  So much fun and energy.

trip_context: {"Wait time": "No wait"}
text:
Hue Walking Street is such a fun and lively place to visit. The atmosphere is super vibrant, especially in the evening. There are many bars and restaurants on higher floors where you can enjoy drinks or food while overlooking the walking street below, and all at very reasonable prices.

You’ll find everything here: street performances, hotels, restaurants, bars, shops, pharmacies, pool table bars… it really has it all.

The energy continues late into the night (or early morning!), making it a great place to hang out, explore, and soak up the local vibe.

Definitely worth a visit when you’re in Hue!

trip_context: {"Visited on": "Weekday", "Wait time": "No wait", "Reservation recommended": "No"}
text: Although the experience and atmosphere is not the same as in Hoi An, it’s good to also have these motorbike- and car-free walking streets in Hue. That way you can stroll safely through these streets and explore the nice restaurants and souvenir shops / vendors. Mind you though that there is also quite some noise and loud music coming from different bars.

Must visit this place if you’re in Hue.
Vibrant, loud and great fun - although we were there during TET celebrations (Lunar New Year).

Great vibe, lots of choice in terms of where you choose to eat or drink and literally everyone wants your custom…

Great atmosphere and good fun!

text: Nguyen Dinh Chieu Walking Street is a short walkway along one side of the Perfume River.  February 3 Park boarders the other side. The street wasn't overly wide. I enjoyed walking along it as you could take in all the sites. It had a great view of the river and the northern banks. The street was smoothly paved which made for an easy, leisurely walk. There were some restaurants and cafes along the street as well as some street food stalls. In the evening, you could do a boat tour of the river.

Came in because of the recommendations. Unfortunately as others have said, the pizza base tastes like a frozen one (nicely cooked, but not like a freshly made dough pizza), two of the three beers I had were a little disappointing (nicely cooked nose but weak on the follow through), and to top it off got charged more than the menu in front of me. Staff were very apologetic, but when they showed me another menu, at least two beers on their menu were marked at a higher price than on the menu they gave me. Luckily I’m gracious… that might not play so well with everyone. Disappointing, because the first beer was good, the tacos weren’t bad and the atmosphere was good. I hope you can pick things up, because there’s a lot of potential.

Postscript: came back at the invitation of the owner, situation nicely rectified. Had another couple of beers, and a nice chat with the owner and the brewer. The Citra Crush was a very nice hazy pale ale. Classy response from the venue… hope to visit again, and maybe get to drink the gose I suggested to the head brewer.
owner_reply:
Hey Christopher, thanks for coming by and sorry you had a disappointing experience.

About the pizza dough, we kneed out each fresh dough ball on the counter in the middle of the restaurant (it's visible in the 4th picture you posted). It definitely isn't coming out of the freezer.

We update our beer list about twice a week and unfortunately there was a typo on yesterday's English version (but not the Vietnamese version, which is the "other" menu they showed you). The prices on the tap board itself were also the correct ones. The staff should have offered you the price on the menu you received even though it's incorrect. That's on us, and thanks for being gracious about that. We've already talked about this with the bar staff to make sure that any future issues always get settled in the customer's favour. It's our mistake after all.

You're also welcome to taste as many beers as you like before ordering so you can choose something that you're excited to drink. This is printed on the menu as well 😉

text:
I don't wish to sound too negative, as we had a nice relaxing time, to a point.

The place is marketed as a 'beach club' and in our experience a beach club has comfortable loungers around a pool, sun shade, music and of course food and drinks.
The first thing that shocked us when we arrived.... zero sun shade....There is not a single umbrella or sunshade anywhere around the pool and coming from Australia where skin cancer is common, we were forced to sit in the direct sunshine.
We paid the entrance fee 150k VND per person and if you want to use the pool, you must pay another 100k VND.... Sorry, but at a beach club anywhere in the world, this is ridiculous, you are going there for the pool and ambiance, why is there an extra fee (abelit very cheap) to use the pool?

I do not have an issue paying an entrance fee, especially when you get 100% back in food and beverage, but as I detailed above, no sunshade, extra fee to cool off in the pool, no music.... I just feel it wasn't good enough for a 5 stars review.

text:
A fantastic Japanese-style cocktail bar with the level of precision and craftsmanship you would expect. From the mixologists in elegant two- and three-piece suits to the exacting way both classics and signatures are prepared and served, everything feels deliberate and refined.

My wife ordered a simple Amaretto Sour, which was anything but simple — made with fresh egg whites and house-made bitters, it was incredibly creamy and perfectly balanced. I had the Ikigai: coffee-infused gin topped with matcha foam. Truly exceptional and unlike anything I’ve had before.

The only disappointment was that foreign credit cards were not accepted, which limited us to one round as we were short on cash. That aside, these are the best cocktails I’ve had in Vietnam so far, without question.
owner_reply:
Thank you so much, Otto, for taking the time to share such a thoughtful and detailed review. We’re truly happy to know that you and your wife enjoyed the cocktails, the service, and the attention to detail — that’s exactly the spirit we aim to bring to every guest.

We’d just like to clarify one small detail: the bitters used in the Amaretto Sour are not house-made. We simply transfer them into small dropper bottles to ensure easier handling and precise dosing during service.

We also appreciate your note regarding payment, and it’s something we’re taking seriously as we work to improve the overall experience.

We hope to welcome you back again soon — and next time, please let us know, we’d be more than happy to prepare a few more special drinks for you. Wishing you a wonderful time in Vietnam.
